9.en: After the pattern. This shows that though the workmanship was man’s the plan was God’s. God has ever counted upon human agencies to cooperate in the building of His house. In this work every individual may have the satisfaction of taking part. In the mount Moses saw “a miniature representation” of the heavenly sanctuary (PP 343; Acts 7:44; Heb. 8:5), the “true tabernacle” (Heb. 8:2). The one on earth is said to be a “pattern” of “heavenly things” (Heb. 9:23, 24) because it was made “according to the pattern” shown to Moses (Heb. 8:5). It was a “copy” of the “great original” in heaven (GC 414). In vision John was ushered into the heavenly sanctuary (Rev. 15:5), where he saw the ark (Rev. 11:19), the altar of incense (Rev. 8:3–5), and possibly the candlestick (Rev. 1:12; 11:4). There is, thus, “indisputable proof of the existence of a sanctuary in heaven,” where the Ruler of the universe sits enthroned (GC 415) and where Christ ministers as our great high priest (Heb. 8:1, 2). It is futile, however, to speculate as to the dimensions, exact appearance, or precise arrangement of the heavenly sanctuary, for “no earthly structure could represent its vastness and its glory” (PP 357). Man is “in the image of God” (Gen. 1:27), yet only Christ is “the express image of his person” (Heb. 1:3). Anything finite can at best but dimly resemble that which is infinite. Moses was shown not the heavenly sanctuary itself, but a representation of it. The earthly sanctuary was patterned after that in heaven to the extent that it was a vivid representation of the various aspects of Christ’s ministry on behalf of fallen man (PP 357). We should focus our attention on what He is doing for us there, as Paul does in Hebrews (Heb. 3:1; 10:12, 19–22; etc.). The tabernacle in heaven, like that on earth, was set up to deal with sin. Christ “entered upon His mediatorial work” after His resurrection and prior to His ascension 40 days later (DA 819). He was prepared to take up His priestly ministry by virtue of having obtained redemption for us through His blood (Heb. 9:12). Solomon knew that even his Temple, though it excelled the wilderness tabernacle in size and beauty, could not contain God (1 Kings 8:27). Yet God owned it as His house (Isa. 56:7), as He later did Herod’s Temple (Matt. 21:31). And He who dwells “in the high and holy place” will take up His abode “with him also that is of a contrite and humble spirit” (Isa. 57:15).
9.zh:
製造帳幕和其中的一切器具都要照我所指示你的樣式。

這說明儘管手藝是人的，但設計卻是上帝的。上帝一直希望人在建造祂居所的事上與祂合作。每一個人都可以參與這項工作。
摩西在山上看見天上聖所的“縮影”（《先祖與先知》第343頁；徒7:44；來8:5）。天上的聖所乃是“真帳幕”（來8:2）。地上的聖所被說成是“天上的本物”的“樣式”（來9:23,24）因為這是“照著”指示摩西的“樣式”做成的（來8:5）。這是天上“偉大的原型”的“一個副本”（《善惡之爭》第414頁）。約翰在異象中曾被帶到天上的聖所（啟15:5）。在那裡他看到了約櫃（啟11:19），香壇（啟8:3-5），可能還有燈臺（啟1:12；11:4）。這樣我們就有“一個無法辯駁的憑據，證明天上是有一個聖所的”（《善惡之爭》第415頁）。宇宙的主宰在那裡作王；基督也在那裡擔任我們的大祭司（來8:1,2）。
但是猜測天上聖所的大小，精確外觀或內部的詳細布置是沒有意義的，因為其“偉大和榮耀，是任何地上的建築所不能代表的”（《 先祖與先知》第357頁）。人是“照著上帝的形象”造成的（創1:27），但只有基督是“上帝本體的真象”（來1:3）。任何有限的事物最多隻能隱約地表現那無限的事物。摩西所看到的不是天上聖所本身，而是一個模型。地上的聖所是照著天上聖所的樣式造的，為了表現基督為墮落人類所作的各方面服務（《先祖與先知》第357頁）。我們應當把注意力集中在祂在那裡為我們所做的事上，正如保羅在《希伯來書》中所說那樣（來3:1；10:12,19-22等）。
天上的帳幕和地上的帳幕都是為對付罪而設立的。基督復活之後到祂四十天後昇天之前，就“已著手進行中保的工作”（《歷代願望》第819頁）。祂藉著寶血所成就的救贖準備好擔任祭司的工作（來9:12）。
所羅門知道他的聖殿雖然在規模和華麗方面遠勝過曠野的帳幕，卻無法容納上帝（王上8:27）。然而上帝仍承認它是自己的居所（賽56:7），正如祂後來對希律聖殿的稱呼（太21:13）。那“住在至高至聖的所在”的主“與心靈痛悔謙卑的人同居”（賽57:15）。
**懷愛倫註釋**。《善惡之爭》413；《救贖的故事》153。

16.en: The testimony. That is, the two tables of stone containing the Ten Commandments (chs. 30:6; 31:18; 32:15, 16). The main purpose of the ark was to serve as a repository for the holy law of God. Because the tables of stone were a transcript of the character and will of God, and were, furthermore, inscribed by God’s own hand, they were honored as the most sacred object in the sanctuary. The latter was therefore called the “tabernacle of testimony” (Ex. 38:21; Num. 9:15; etc.). The law was also known as “the covenant” (Deut. 4:12, 13; 9:9–15), and the ark was therefore commonly called the “ark of the covenant” (Deut. 31:26; Heb. 9:4; etc.).
16.zh:
必將我所要賜給你的法版放在櫃裡。

**法版。**就是寫有十條誡命的兩塊石版（出30:6；31:18；32:15,16）。櫃主要用來放置上帝神聖的律法。石版是上帝品格和旨意的寫照，而且是上帝親手所寫的，所以被視為聖所中最神聖的物件。聖所因此被稱為“法的帳幕”（出38:21；民9:15等）。律法也稱為“約”（申4:12,13；9:9-15），故櫃通常稱為“約櫃”（申31:26；來9:4等）。
**懷愛倫註釋**。《先祖與先知》349；《救贖的故事》153，183。
**懷愛倫註釋（16–21節）**。《先祖與先知》348。

18.en: Cherubims. More accurately, “cherubim,” the Hebrew plural for “cherub.” The derivation of the word is uncertain. The cherubim were attached to the mercy seat, one at either end (see Gen. 3:24). One wing of each angel was stretched forth on high, and the other was folded over his body (see Eze. 1:11) in token of reverence and humility. The position of the cherubim with their faces turned toward each other and directed downward toward the ark, represented the reverence with which the heavenly host regard the law of God, and their interest in the plan of redemption.
18.zh:
要用金子錘出兩個基路伯來，安在施恩座的兩頭。

“基路伯”一詞來歷不明。基路伯安在施恩座上，一邊一個（見創3:24）。每位天使的一隻翅膀高高地伸出來，另一隻翅膀則收起來遮蓋自己的身體（見結1:11），象徵崇敬和謙卑。基路伯的臉彼此相對並向下朝著約櫃，象徵天軍對上帝律法的尊重，以及他們對救贖計劃的關注。

17.en: A mercy seat. The word thus translated is from a root meaning “to cover,” that is, “to pardon” sin. It represented divine mercy. Significantly, it was of “pure gold,” implying that mercy is the most precious of God’s attributes. It was placed over the law, inasmuch as mercy transcends justice (Ps. 85:10; 89:14). The ark with its justice and the mercy seat with its mercy were both needed to reveal the full character of God’s dealings with men. Mercy without justice is weak sentimentality, subversive of all moral order. On the other hand, justice without mercy is moral severity, theoretically without a flaw, but revolting to both God and man. The ark and the mercy seat constituted the very heart of the sanctuary. Above the mercy seat was the Shekinah, the symbol of the divine presence. The tables of the law within the ark testified to the fact that God’s kingdom is founded on an immutable standard of righteousness (Ps. 97:2), which even divine grace must respect. Grace cannot be dispensed on terms which “make void the law” (Rom. 3:31). When sin is pardoned, the law’s claim against the sinner must also be satisfied. The very purpose of the gospel is to secure for the sinner the forgiveness of his sins, by faith in a means that does not “make void the law,” but “establishes” it. While the tables within the ark testified against the people, the mercy seat pointed to a way in which the claims of the law could be met and the sinner saved from death, the penalty of the law. On the basis of law alone there can be no reunion between God and man, since sin separates us from Him (Isa. 59:1, 2). The blood-sprinkled mercy seat must intervene, for it is only on the ground of Christ’s mediation on our behalf that we can draw near to God (Heb. 7:25).
17.zh:
要用精金做施恩座（施恩：或作蔽罪；下同），長二肘半，寬一肘半。

“施恩座”源於詞根“覆蓋”，即“寬恕”罪孽。它象徵上帝的憐憫。值得注意的是，這是用“精金”作的，暗示著憐憫是上帝最寶貴的品性。它被安放在律法上方，說明憐憫超越公義（詩85:10；89:14）。櫃及其公義，施恩座及其憐憫，都是彰顯上帝待人的完美品格所必需的。沒有公義的憐憫是情感的懦弱，違背一切道德的規則。而沒有憐憫的公義則是道德上的苛刻，理論上無懈可擊，但不為上帝和人類所喜愛。
櫃和施恩座構成了聖所的核心。在施恩座上方乃是榮光，是上帝臨格的象徵。櫃中的法版表明上帝的國是建立在不可改變的公義標準之上的（詩97:2），就連上帝的恩典也必須尊重此律法。恩典的施與不能以“廢了律法”為條件（羅3:31）。當罪得到寬恕時，律法對罪人的要求也必須被滿足。福音的根本目的就是確保罪人因信而獲得赦免，不是“廢了律法”，而是“堅固律法”。櫃中的石版雖然作了不利於百姓的證言，但施恩座指出了一條使律法的要求得以滿足並拯救罪人脫離律法的承罰，就是死亡的途徑。人單靠律法是無法與上帝和好的，因為罪使我們與祂隔絕（賽59:1,2）。必須有灑上血的施恩座的介入，因為只有基督作我們作中保，我們才能親近上帝（來7:25）。
**懷愛倫註釋（17–20節）**。《救贖的故事》153。

8.en: Make me a sanctuary. Though the Hebrews knew, as we know, that the great God could not possibly “dwell” in any building made by men (1 Kings 8:27; 2 Chron. 2:6; Isa. 66:1; Jer. 23:23, 24), it did not seem appropriate that there should be worship without a temple. Furthermore, the sanctuary provided a visible center for the worship of the one true God, and was thus a bulwark against the worship of the many gods of the heathen. It brought God near to His people and made His presence among them real. This too was a protection against idolatry (Ex. 29:43, 45; (Num. 35:34). Inasmuch as at that time the Israelites were a nomadic, a wandering people, the sanctuary was to be a tent that could easily be dismantled and moved from place to place. It is significant that the Hebrew word for “sanctuary” is never applied to a heathen temple. That I may dwell. In a spiritual sense, God has ever sought an abode with men and cannot “rest” until this has been accorded Him (Ps. 132:13–16), first in the hearts of His people individually (1 Cor. 3:16, 17; 6:19) and then in the midst of any company who meet to worship Him (Matt. 18:20). The system centering in the earthly tabernacle pointed forward to Christ, who later “dwelt,” literally “tabernacled,” among men (John 1:14). The Hebrew word shakan, “dwell,” means to be a permanent resident in a community. It is closely related to the word Shekinah, used of the manifestation of divine glory that took up its abode above the mercy seat PP 349). The Shekinah was the symbol of the divine presence, in which God promised to “dwell among them” (see Ex. 25:22).
8.zh:
又當為我造聖所，使我可以住在他們中間。

**當為我造聖所。**雖然希伯來人和我們一樣，都知道偉大的上帝不可能住在任何人手所造的建築中（王上8:27；代下2:6；賽66:1；耶23:23,24），但沒有聖殿的敬拜似乎是不合適的。另外，聖所還提供了敬拜獨一真神的一個看得見的中心，從而成為防止敬拜異教諸神的堡壘。聖所使上帝就近祂的子民，實現祂與他們同在。這也是偶像崇拜的防禦措施（出29:43,45；民35:34）。以色列人當時是一個遊牧民族，所以聖所應是一個易於拆卸和搬運的帳棚。值得注意的是，表示“聖所”的希伯來詞語從未用來指異教的神廟。
**使我可以住。**從屬靈意義上說，上帝一直都在尋找與人同在的居所，得到以後祂才“安息”（詩132:13-16）。首先祂是住在每一個子民的心中（林前3:16,17；6:19），然後是住在每一個聚集敬拜祂的團體中（太18:20）。以屬世的帳幕為中心的制度預表後來“住在”、或直譯為“支搭帳幕”在人類中間（約1:14）的基督。
希伯來語shakan指在一個地方的永久住所，與表示施恩座上方上帝榮光的詞彙Shekinah有密切的聯繫（《先祖與先知》第349頁）。上帝榮光是上帝同在的象徵，上帝應許要“住在他們中間”（見出25:22）。
**懷愛倫註釋**。《歷代願望》23；《教育論》35；《善惡之爭》411，413；居61；《先祖與先知》313，343；《證言》卷四78。

2.zh:
你告訴以色列人當為我送禮物來；凡甘心樂意的，你們就可以收下歸我。

**為我送禮物。**上帝的旨意已經在十誡中向以色列人顯明瞭。“約書”的律法和“典章”也已賜給了摩西，上帝與祂子民之間已經立約。但崇拜的固定形式尚未確定。迄今只有“壇”已被採用並獲得了某些相關指示（出20:24-26），但還沒有制定完整的制度，可以使敬拜獨一真神成為百姓與祂親密交往並順從祂，防止他們敬拜異教諸神的有效手段。百姓應有權參與建造上帝在他們中間的居所。
**甘心樂意的。**上帝只要出於內心的奉獻，而不只是出於雙手或錢包。祂只接受“甘心樂意”的禮物（林後9:6,7）。只有用心捐獻的人，名字才錄在上帝貨單上，因為他們是本著馬其頓教會的精神捐獻的（林後8:1-5）。出35:21-29和36:3-7記錄了百姓以這種方式的回應。他們回應得非常積極，以至被“攔住……不再拿”。因此帳幕是樂意奉獻的產物。在大衛時代準備建造聖殿時，百姓表現出同樣的精神（代上29:1-9）。後來被擄者和所羅巴伯一起從巴比倫回來重建聖殿時，他們也是這樣奉獻的（拉2:68,69；該1:12-14）。
**懷愛倫註釋**。《給管家的勉言》203；《先知與君王》61；《先祖與先知》343；《證言》卷四78。

3.zh:
所要收的禮物：就是金、銀、銅，

這三種金屬用於建造帳幕本身和其中的器具。“銅”是銅錫合金，因此是青銅而不是黃銅。希伯來人離開埃及時，曾向埃及人“要”過財物（見出3:22；12:35,36註釋）。百姓將他們最好的財物獻給耶和華。上帝不接受“瞎眼”、“瘸腿”、或“有病”的“祭物”（瑪1:8）。這並不是說上帝要我們作力所不能及的奉獻，而是要我們盡己所能（林後8:12）。
寡婦的“小錢”（可12:41-44），“一玉瓶極貴的香膏”（太26:6-13），和放在使徒腳前田產的“價銀”（徒5:1,2）一樣蒙祂悅納。把我們最好的獻給上帝不但指財物，也指我們的才能，光陰和精力。我們最優秀的能力，最熱烈的情感，最深刻思想，最高尚的願望都應是屬於祂的。在基督的侍奉中需要各種各樣的禮物。沒有一個人會因太貧窮或無能而不能履行自己的本分。我們不要忘記那只有一千銀子之人的失敗所帶給我們的教訓（太25:14,15,24-30）。以色列人藉著獻身於上帝的聖工和事奉祂而將財寶積攢在天上（太6:19-21）。他們沒有被世界的“益處”所欺騙，因為他們不想“賠上”來生來“賺得”世界（見太16:25,26）。

5.zh:
染紅的公羊皮，海狗皮，皂莢木，

**海狗皮。**該詞原文似乎來埃及語，指某一種動物的皮；也有人認為該詞源於一個阿拉伯詞語，指“海豹”類，特別是儒艮或海牛（《先祖與先知》第347頁）。這種海生食草類哺乳動物身長3至3.6米，長著圓圓的腦袋，以母乳餵養幼崽，有分叉的尾巴，經常出沒在紅海的珊瑚礁中間。據推測是儒艮引發了美人魚的傳說。“海狗”皮成了帳幕的外層遮蓋。
**皂莢木。**就是洋槐木。這種木材堅硬，耐久，紋理細密，適合於製作櫥櫃。

10.zh:
要用皂莢木做一櫃，長二肘半，寬一肘半，高一肘半。

**一櫃。**該詞詞根的含義可能是“收集”、“聚集”。若是這樣，“櫃”就是保管物品的。一個相關的亞述詞aranu（“箱子”），就是來自詞根aramu（“覆蓋”）。
**一肘。**和埃及人一樣，希伯來人既使用長肘又使用短肘。雖然不知道希伯來肘的長度，但人們卻知道埃及的普通肘是45釐米，御肘是52釐米。這兩種肘希伯來人肯定都是瞭解的，因為他們曾參與埃及城市的建造。在以西結的時代，希伯來人使用的肘約長44.5釐米（見本卷註釋第165頁），接近於埃及的普通肘，因此我們可以假定建造帳幕所使用的就是這種肘。故此櫃應長約1.11米，寬和高約0.67米。
**懷愛倫註釋（10–11節）**。《善惡之爭》412；《救贖的故事》153，183。
**懷愛倫註釋（10–15節）**。《先祖與先知》348。

12.zh:
也要鑄四個金環，安在櫃的四腳上；這邊兩環，那邊兩環。

金環不是安在上面的“角”上，而是安在四個“腳”或“座”上（參第22節）。有“槓”穿過這些環（第13節）。在以色列飄流的時期由扛櫃之人的肩膀抬著。這些“槓”要留在環中（第15節），免得人在安放或抬起櫃時觸到櫃的任何部位。由於這些“槓”不屬櫃子，觸摸或搬運都不算褻瀆（見撒下6:6,7）。

21.zh:
要將施恩座安在櫃的上邊，又將我所要賜給你的法版放在櫃裡。

**懷愛倫註釋**。《善惡之爭》413。

22.zh:
我要在那裡與你相會，又要從法櫃施恩座上二基路伯中間，和你說我所要吩咐你傳給以色列人的一切事。

**懷愛倫註釋**。《基督教育原理》253；《先祖與先知》349。

23.zh:
要用皂莢木做一張桌子，長二肘，寬一肘，高一肘半。

**用皂莢木作一張桌子。**摩西現在從至聖所轉到描述聖所的器具。首先提到的是“陳設餅”的桌子。“陳設餅”（可2:26）是呈獻給上帝的餅。保羅在來9:2中也使用了該詞。桌子的規格約為88.9 x 44.5 x 66.7釐米。見出25:10註釋。當人進入帳幕時，這張桌子應該在右邊或北邊（出40:22）。
**懷愛倫註釋（23–25節）**。《先祖與先知》348。

24.zh:
要包上精金，四圍鑲上金牙邊。

**四圍鑲上金牙邊。**這是桌面四圍防止物品掉下來的邊框或嵌線。約瑟弗斯說“四個環”（第26節）安在桌子的腳上，從其中穿抬桌子的“槓”（《上古史》iii.6.6）。

29.zh:
要做桌子上的盤子、調羹，並奠酒的爵和瓶；這都要用精金製作。

**盤子。**可能是用來裝餅的。“調羹”指燒香的杯或壺，就像提多門的桌子浮雕上所顯示的。該拱門是為記念公元70年攻陷耶路撒冷而在羅馬豎立起來的。“爵”和“瓶”用於和素祭同獻的奠祭（利23:13,18,37等）。
**奠。**直譯為“倒出”。

30.zh:
又要在桌子上，在我面前，常擺陳設餅。

“陳設餅”共有12個，每安息日更換一次。換下的餅被視為聖物，由祭司在“聖所”中吃掉（利24:5-9）。這12個餅象徵12個支派因每天從祂那裡領受的生命之福而不斷向上帝獻上的感恩祭。從更高的意義上說，該餅指的是屬靈耶穌基督。
**懷愛倫註釋**。《善惡之爭》412；《先祖與先知》354。

31.zh:
要用精金做一個燈臺。燈臺的座和幹與杯、球、花，都要接連一塊錘出來。

正如提多門所顯示並由的約瑟弗斯所證實的（《上古史》iii.6.7），“燈臺”有一個垂直的軸，向兩邊分出三對（第35節）分枝，均與燈頂平齊。沒有說明尺寸，但它是用純金作的。其分枝上有杏仁狀的“杯”（第33節）；有“球”，或柱頭，據有些聖經學者說象石榴；還有“花”。“燈臺”的燈在日落時會逐一修剪，次日早晨再次修剪（出27:20,21；30:7,8；利24:3,4）。它們決不可同時熄滅（《先祖與先知》第348頁）。當祭司進入帳幕的第一層時，燈臺在他的左邊朝南的位置（出40:24）。
**懷愛倫註釋**。《善惡之爭》348。

37.zh:
要做燈臺的七個燈盞。祭司要點這燈，使燈光對照。

**懷愛倫註釋**。《善惡之爭》412。

38.zh:
燈臺的蠟剪和蠟花盤也是要精金的。

“蠟剪”是用來修剪燈芯的鉗子或剪子。“蠟花盤”用來收集“蠟剪”剪下來的燈芯碎片。

39.zh:
做燈臺和這一切的器具要用精金一他連得。

一他連得相當於34.19公斤。體積應為1772.4立方厘米，可以製成一個邊長略大於4-3/4英寸的立方體（1756.52立方厘米）。從某種意義上說，“燈臺”象徵上帝的百姓以個人身份（太5:14-16；腓2:15）和作為一個教會（啟1:12,20）在世界上作道德和屬靈的光，也象徵聖靈啟迪教會的能力（亞4:2-6；啟4:5）。但如上所述，從最高的意義上說，它代表我們主救主耶穌基督（約9:5）。祂是世界的光（約1:4；8:12；12:46），把來自“眾光之父”的“各樣美善的恩賜和各樣全備的賞賜”（雅1:17）賜給人。

40.zh:
要謹慎做這些物件，都要照著在山上指示你的樣式。

**懷愛倫註釋**。《使徒行述》564；《基督教育之研究》60，《教育論》25.258；《善惡之爭》413；《先祖與先知》343，356；《救贖的故事》153，《證言》卷五549。

19.en: Moses spake. So awful was the sight, the mount being covered with smoke (v. 18), and so fearful the sound of the trumpet (v. 16), that Moses could not remain silent. To relieve the tension he broke forth in words, perhaps those recorded in Heb. 12:21. There is suggested a profound meaning in the words “Moses spake, and God answered,” which offer a striking definition of the nature of divine law. All God’s commands are, so to speak, responses to our deep soul needs. They issue forth from the reciprocal action of God and the human heart. Paul in Rom. 7 illustrates this. Man, by his very creation in the image of God (Gen. 1:27), can never find satisfaction in being alive unless his life is in tune with the Creator. The Decalogue is the tuning instrument. It is not simply a code expressing the will and the sovereignty of God; it is also an instrument of spiritual instruction to help us live as God intends that we should (Ps. 19:7, 8; 119:97, 98; Matt. 19:16, 17).
19.zh:
角聲漸漸地高而又高，摩西就說話，神有聲音答應他。

當時的場面十分可畏。山被煙霧所籠罩（第18節）；號筒的聲音非常可怕（第16節）。摩西再也不能保持沉默。為了消除緊張的氣氛，他開始說話，可能就是來12:21所記的話。有人認為“摩西就說話，上帝有聲音答應他”這句話有著深刻的含義，為上帝律法的性質提供了明確的定義。上帝的一切命令實際上都是為了回應我們內心的需求，是出於上帝和人心的交流活動。保羅在《羅馬書》第7章中說明了這一點。人類是按照上帝形象所造的（創1:27）。他在生存中永遠得不到滿足，除非他的生命與創造主保持和諧。十誡所起的是調節的作用。它不只是一部表達上帝旨意和權威的法典，也是幫助我們按照上帝的旨意生活、進行屬靈教導的工具（詩19:7,8；119:97,98；太19:16,17）。

11.en: Come down. Generally in the Bible, God is represented as dwelling in the heavens above (1 Kings 8:30, 49; John 8:23). Therefore, when He appears on the earth He is said to “come down” (Gen. 11:5–7; 18:21; Ex. 3:8).
11.zh:
到第三天要預備好了，因為第三天耶和華要在眾百姓眼前降臨在西乃山上。

聖經一般描述上帝住在天上（王上8:30,49；約8:23）。所以祂在地上顯現，就說成是“降臨”（創11:5-7；18:21；出3:8）。
**懷愛倫註釋**。《基督教育原理》506。

8.en: All that the Lord hath spoken. Convinced and assured in their hearts that the terms of the covenant would be just and good, and desirous of securing for themselves and their posterity the blessings the Lord had promised, the elders readily accepted the covenant before knowing what its exact provisions would be. It was desirable that the people should express willingness to enter into such a covenant as God proposed, and to have time to think the matter through before being called to make formal ratification of it. If they were willing to obey God, the details of the covenant would follow. Nevertheless, while there was no doubt a noble desire on the part of the Israelites to respond to God’s call for obedience, they entered into the covenant relationship with but little knowledge of themselves and with no appreciation of their inability to keep the divine precepts and thus fulfill their part of the agreement. Like so many deceived souls, they thought they had but to try in order to do. God permitted the attempt in order that they might discover their inability and so be led to rely upon God. Paul’s own experience is a pertinent case in point (see Rom. 7). The spontaneous cry, “All that the Lord hath spoken we will do,” was without question a superficial demonstration of religious enthusiasm, a momentary reaction to a glorious and sublime truth. There was lacking the spirit of deep, true conversion, the “heart” to do what God demanded (Deut. 5:29). It is small wonder the people soon apostatized, and worshiped the golden calf (Ex. 32).
8.zh:
百姓都同聲回答說：凡耶和華所說的，我們都要遵行。摩西就將百姓的話回覆耶和華。

眾長老確信聖約的條款是公正良善的，又渴望使自己和後代獲得耶和華所應許的福氣，就在瞭解聖約的具體規定之前欣然接受了它。百姓應該表示訂立上帝所提之約的願望，並在蒙召正式簽訂以前花時間認真思考。如果他們願意順從上帝，聖約的細節就會隨之而來。但雖然以色列人對上帝順從之呼召的回應無疑表達了一種高尚的願望，但他們在立約時對自己並不太瞭解，也沒有認識到他們無法遵守上帝的命令，履行聖約的義務。和許多糊塗的人一樣，他們認為要做就得先嚐試。上帝允許這種嘗試，為了使他們能發現自己的無能，從而轉過來依靠上帝。保羅的經驗就是一個典型的事例（見羅7章）。
**“凡耶和華所說的，我們都要遵行”。**這句脫口而出的回答無疑是宗教熱情的膚淺表現；是對光榮真理的一時反應，缺少深刻真誠的悔改精神，缺乏遵行上帝要求的“心”（申5:29）。怪不得百姓很快就背道去拜金牛犢了（出32）。
**懷愛倫註釋**。《基督教育原理》506；《先知與君王》293；《先祖與先知》303。

17.en: Brought forth the people. It is evident that the camp itself must have been back some distance from the foot of the mount, with an open space between the first tents and the barrier that Moses had erected close to the mount. Into this vacant space Moses now led the people, thus bringing them as near as they dared approach the divine presence.
17.zh:
摩西率領百姓出營迎接神，都站在山下。

營地本身顯然離山腳有一段距離。在第一排帳棚和摩西在山腳所立的圍欄之間有一片空地。摩西現在率領百姓進入這塊空地，儘量接近上帝臨格之處。

13.en: Not an hand touch it. Or, “No hand shall touch him” (RSV). The one transgressing the divine command was not to be seized, for the one making the arrest would have to pass the “bounds” in order to do so. Instead, the transgressor was to be killed by stones thrown or arrows shot from within the “bounds.” The same was to be done to any beast that strayed into the restricted area, lest anyone be tempted to enter the restricted area to retrieve his stray animal. Everything was done to impress the Israelites with the awful majesty of God, and the spirit of solemnity that should fill one’s heart upon approaching the divine presence. God is ever present (Ps. 139:1–12), but He veils His presence. Though He is with us we do not perceive Him (Job 23:8, 9). But when He does reveal His presence, all tremble before Him (Gen. 28:16, 17; Job 42:5, 6; Hab. 3:16). Weakness quakes before strength, littleness shrinks before greatness, finite man becomes insignificant in the presence of the Infinite. It is consciousness of sin that makes a man tremble before a holy God (Gen. 3:10). Corruption quails before incorruption, moral depravity before absolute purity. They shall come up. The pronoun “they” cannot here refer to the people, for this would contradict the command of the previous verse. The people never did ascend the mount. But Moses, Aaron, Nadab, Abihu, and the 70 elders did (see Ex. 24:1, 2), and they are probably the ones here referred to.
13.zh:
不可用手摸他，必用石頭打死，或用箭射透；無論是人是牲畜，都不得活。到角聲拖長的時候，他們才可到山根來。

**不可用手摸他。**不要去抓干犯上帝命令的人，因為捉拿的人將不得不越過“界限”才能成功。所以應當從“界限”內拋擲石頭或射箭處死罪犯。闖入禁區的牲畜也要同樣處理，免得有人受試探進入禁區去取回他走失的牲畜。這一切都是為了使以色列人認識到上帝可畏的尊嚴。每一個人在接近上帝時都應充滿莊嚴肅穆的精神。
上帝是永遠與人同在的（詩139:1-12），但祂遮蔽了祂的臨格。祂雖然與我們同在，我們卻覺察不到（伯23:8, 9）。但一旦祂顯示顯現，眾人都在祂面前戰慄（創28:16,17；伯42:5, 6；哈3:16）。軟弱在強壯麵前顫抖；渺小在偉大面前畏縮；有限的人類在無限的主面前顯得微不足道。負疚感使人在聖潔的上帝面前戰驚（創3:10）。腐敗在廉潔面前畏縮；道德敗壞在完全的純潔面前膽怯。
**他們才可到山根來。**“他們”不可能指百姓，因為這與前一節的命令相矛盾。百姓從未上過山。只有摩西，亞倫，拿答，亞比戶和七十位長老上過山（見出24:1,2）。“他們”可能是指這些人。

20.en: The top of the mount. Probably not Jebel Musa, which was invisible from the plain where the people must have been assembled, but Ras es–Safsaf, the highest eminence of the Sinai mountains fronting on the plain (see on v. 1 and on ch. 3:1). Called Moses up. The context would lead us to think that Aaron went up with Moses, for Aaron was present there (v. 24) and is probably included in the “us” of v. 23.
20.zh:
耶和華降臨在西乃山頂上，耶和華召摩西上山頂，摩西就上去。

**山頂上。**可能不是慕薩山（Jebel Musa），因為這座山從百姓聚集的平原上是看不見的；而是西奈山脈的最高峰沙弗沙弗角（Ras es-Safsaf）。它正好朝著該平原（見第1節和出3:1註釋）。
**召摩西上山頂。**據上下文，亞倫和摩西是一同上去的，因為亞倫也在那裡（第24節）。他也可能也包括在23節的“我們”中。
**懷愛倫註釋**。《基督教育原理》237，287，506；《先祖與先知》366；《救贖的故事》148。

5.en: If ye will obey. Rather than command the Hebrews to keep His covenant, as was His sovereign right, God graciously invited His people to do that which would be for their own benefit. The only avenue upon which we can walk with God is that of obedience. On no other terms but obedience could God consent to be their God or to have them for His chosen people. The grace of the gospel of Jesus Christ that brings salvation to all men (Titus 2:11) does not release them from their obligation to obey the divine law (Rom. 3:31). Faith in the redeeming Christ is inseparably joined to the power of the indwelling Christ, which enables one to keep the Ten Commandments (Rom. 8:1–4). Jesus and the apostles most emphatically affirmed the principle of obedience to divine law (Matt. 5:17, 18; 19:16, 17; 1 Cor. 7:19; James 1:25; 2:10–12; 1 John 2:3, 4). My covenant. The covenant God made with Israel at Sinai is generally called the “old covenant” (Heb. 8:13). Owing to the failure of the people to appreciate fully the purpose of God and to enter into the true spirit of the covenant, it stood forth in contrast to the new, or gospel, covenant as follows: (1) It was more elementary (Gal. 4:1–5). (2) It was more closely related to outward rites and ceremonies (Heb. 9:1). (3) Its motives were largely penalties and rewards, for, as “children,” these were the only incentives Israel was yet prepared to understand (Gal. 4:3; PP 371). (4) Its blessings were largely temporal. (5) It trusted in human accomplishment and good works rather than in divine grace and a Saviour from sin (see on Ex. 19:8). The signal blessing of the new covenant is that through faith in Christ, power is imparted to the believer to fulfill “the righteousness of the law” (Rom. 8:1–4; cf. Acts 13:37–39). God permitted Israel to attempt to keep the law, so they might become aware of their inability to do what they mistakenly felt able to do. They would thus be led from trust in self to trust in God, from confidence in their own endeavors to faith in divine accomplishment. Thus, the law would become the means of leading them to Christ as their only Saviour from sin (Gal. 3:23–26). Thus, the way was prepared for the new covenant relationship, the gospel of divine grace, the law kept in and through Christ (Jer. 31:31–34; Rom. 3:21–31; 8:1–4; Heb. 8:7–11). As Paul declares, this new covenant relationship does not “make void the law through faith” (Rom. 3:31). The law remains the standard of duty, the norm of holy practice. The new covenant establishes the law as the eternal code of righteousness, without which there can be no holy conduct. A peculiar treasure. Rather, “my own possession” (RSV; see also Ps. 135:4; Isa. 43:1–4). In the sight of God no other nation was equal to Israel. Every child of God, every consecrated Christian, is a jewel in the crown of our Lord, and is so considered by Him (Mal. 3:17; see on 1 Peter 2:9).
5.zh:
如今你們若實在聽從我的話，遵守我的約，就要在萬民中作屬我的子民，因為全地都是我的。

**你們若實在聽從。**上帝雖然有至高的權利命令希伯來人遵守祂的約，但祂仍親切地邀請祂的子民去做對他們有好處的事情。我們能與上帝同行的唯一道路就是順從的道路。除了順從以外，沒有什麼條件能使上帝同意做他們的上帝，或讓他們做祂的選民。那給眾人帶來救恩的耶穌基督福音的恩惠（多2:11），並不解除他們順服上帝律法的義務（羅3:31）。對救贖主基督的信心是與基督在人心中的大能密不可分的。這種能力會使人遵守十誡（羅8:1-4）。耶穌和使徒們都特別強調順從上帝律法的原則（太5:17,18；19:16,17；林前7:19；雅1:25；2:10-12；約壹2:3,4）。
**我的約。**上帝與以色列人在西奈所立的約一般稱為“舊約”（來8:13）。由於百姓沒有充分認識上帝的旨意，理解該約的真正意義，它就與新約或福音之約形成了以下的對比：一， 它較為初級（加4:1-5）。二。它比較注重外表的禮儀（來9:1）。三，主要靠賞罰來實施，因為作為“孩童”，以色列人只能明白這些方法（加4:3；《先祖與先知》第371頁）。四，其福氣大都是今世的。五，它依靠人的成就和善行，而不是上帝的恩典和救我們脫離罪惡的救主（見出19:8註釋）。新約的顯著福氣就是藉著相信基督，賜能力給信徒以成就“律法的義”（羅8:1-4；參徒13:37-39）。
上帝允許以色列人嘗試遵守律法，為使他們認識到自己做不到他們誤認為能做的事。於是他們的信心就從自己轉到上帝身上，從依靠自己的努力轉到相信上帝的大能。這樣，律法就成為引導他們接受基督為擺脫罪惡唯一救主的工具（加3:23-26）。這就為新約的關係，上帝恩典的福音，在基督裡並藉著基督遵守律法預備了道路（耶31:31-34；羅3:21-31；8:1-4；來8:7-11）。正如保羅所宣稱的，這種新約的關係並不“因信廢了律法”（羅3:31）。律法仍然是責任的標準，聖潔行為的準則。新約確立律法為公義的永恆準則。沒有律法就不可能有聖潔的行為。
**屬我的子民。**就是“我自己的財產”（英文RSV版；又見詩135:4；賽43:1-4）。在上帝的眼中，沒有其他的民族能與以色列人相比。上帝的每一個兒女，每一個獻身的基督徒，都是我們主冠冕上的珍珠；祂也是這樣看的（瑪3:17；見彼前2:9註釋）。
**懷愛倫註釋**。《先知與君王》293。
**懷愛倫註釋（5–6節）**。《先祖與先知》303，371；《證言》卷二450。

12.en: Set bounds. Moses was to erect a barrier of some kind about the base of the mountain. It may have extended along the line of low mounds guarding the foot of the cliff. So long as the people refrained from crossing these “bounds” they were safe. It has been fittingly remarked that Sinai, with all its described terrors, was not Vesuvius; the people beneath were not gathered in a doomed Herculaneum or Pompeii. The purpose of the Lord was simply to manifest the reality, extent, and proximity of His destroying power. Men were made to feel what that power could do, if they were so presumptuous or negligent as to come within its rightful exercise. Whosoever toucheth. Because the cliff rises abruptly from the plain, some might easily come in contact with it, either carelessly or out of curiosity. Be surely put to death. This severe punishment was specifically announced by God to impress upon the people in no uncertain terms what it meant to be in the presence of a holy God. The penalty was fully in keeping with the awful solemnity of the occasion. Further, we should not forget that it was only by sobering threats of punishment that the Israelites, prone at times to be presumptuous and to rebel against the divine will, could be taught reverence (see 2 Sam. 6:6, 7). There can be no true religious feeling without a profound sense of reverence. To inculcate such an attitude among the Israelites, it was imperative to impress the lesson in a dramatic and striking fashion.
12.zh:
你要在山的四圍給百姓定界限，說：你們當謹慎，不可上山去，也不可摸山的邊界；凡摸這山的，必要治死他。

**定界限。**摩西要在山腳豎立某種障礙物。可能是沿著峭壁腳下那些小土墩而設立的。只要百姓不越過“界限”，他們就是安全的。
有人說得好，西奈以及所描述的恐怖，不能與維蘇威火山相比。山下的百姓也不是聚集註定毀滅的赫丘拉紐或龐培。耶和華只是為了顯示其毀滅能力的真實性，廣泛性和迫近性。要讓人認識到，如果他貿然或不經意闖了禁，這種能力將意味著什麼。
**凡摸這山的。**因為峭壁是從平原上突起的，有些人很容易接觸到它，不論是粗心還是出於好奇。
**必要治死他。**上帝特意宣佈這種嚴厲的懲罰，為要讓百姓清楚地認識到在聖潔的上帝面前意味著什麼。這種懲罰完全適合於這莊嚴肅穆的場合。此外我們不要忘記，只有藉著懲罰的嚴肅警告，才會使容易放肆和悖逆上帝旨意的以色列人學會敬畏（見撒下6:6,7）。沒有深深的敬畏感，就不可能有真正的宗教情感。為了在以色列人中培養這種態度，就需要用形象驚人的方式來進行教育。
**懷愛倫註釋（12–13節）**。《歷代願望》156；《先祖與先知》304；《救贖的故事》138。

1.en: In the third month. That is, Sivan, comparable to our late May or early June. Verses 1 and 2 deal with the last stage of the journey of the Israelites to Mt. Sinai. At Mt. Sinai there occurred one of the great events of Jewish history, the incorporation of Israel as a church and a nation under the theocracy (PP 303). This form of government continued until, with the words, “We have no king but Caesar” (John 19:15), the Jews withdrew from it (DA 738). The process of organization at Sinai included the proclamation of the Ten Commandments, the ratification of the covenant, the construction of the tabernacle, the giving of ceremonial and civil laws, and the perfection of various civil and military procedures. A unique relationship was effected between the Lord and the descendants of Abraham, one into which no other nation would ever enter. Its purpose was to prepare the way for the coming of Christ as man’s Saviour. The same day. Literally, “on this very day,” perhaps the first day of Sivan, possibly the 15th. Jewish tradition placed this event on the first day of the third month of the Jewish year. If so, the journey from Rameses to Sinai probably took 45 days. The wilderness of Sinai. This is generally regarded as being the plain er–Raha, a nearly flat, bush-studded plain or desert, approximately 2 mi. long and 1/2 mi. wide (see on ch. 3:1). It was a suitable place for the Hebrews to gather to receive the law God was soon to proclaim, surrounded as it was by mountains which formed a natural amphitheater. At its southeastern end rose an almost perpendicular cliff of granite, which provided a high pulpit, or altar, from which the voice of the Lord might be heard. At the foot of this cliff was a series of low mounds that may have helped determine the “bounds” (v. 12) designed to keep the people from touching the mountain. It was in such a majestic, inspiring environment that the law was given to Israel. It has been well observed that no spot in the world can be pointed out that combines in a more remarkable manner the conditions of a commanding height and of a plain, in every part of which the sights and sounds described in Exodus would reach an assembled multitude. It was a location of solitude, where the people could be entirely alone with God, away from everything that would draw their thought and attention from things divine. For more than 11 months Israel was to remain at Sinai. Here, besides receiving the law and ratifying the covenant, they would have time for the construction of the sanctuary and for the further development of their organization. It would afford them an opportunity for quiet reflection upon their responsibility toward the Lord. God’s people need such periods of rest, as Christ advised the disciples (see Mark 6:31). We have the example of Paul, who himself “went into Arabia,” possibly to this very place (see Gal. 1:17). All of us need our Sinais, where, in quietness and solitude, God can do for us what He did for Israel, revealing His will, instructing us in it, and impressing us anew with His majesty. Sinai was a place of such solemnity that the minds of the people would irresistibly be elevated to communion with the Infinite. The very sternness and grandeur of the surroundings were a fit commentary on the sanctity of the law. As a fruitless, barren desert, Sinai is also a sharp reminder that of ourselves we can bear no spiritual fruit to the glory of God and cannot work out our own salvation. Did not Christ Himself say, “Without me ye can do nothing” (John 15:5)?
1.zh:
以色列人出埃及地以後，滿了三個月的那一天，就來到西乃的曠野。

**滿了三個月。**就是西彎月，相當於五月底或六月初。第1、2節講述以色列人前往西奈山的最後行程。在西奈山發生了猶太人歷史中最大的事件之一，就是以色列人在神權體制下成為一個教會和國家（《先祖與先知》第303頁）。這種政體一直持續到猶太人說“除了該撒，我們沒有王”（約19:15）而退出為止（《歷代願望》第738頁）。在西奈的組建過程包括宣佈十誡，與上帝立約，建造帳幕，頒佈儀文和民事律法，以及完善各種民事和軍事組織。耶和華與亞伯拉罕後裔的特殊關係開始生效。這種關係是一種任何其他國家所沒有的。其目的是為基督作為人類救主的到臨而預備道路。
**那一天。**可能是西彎月初一，也可能是十五日。據猶太教的遺傳，這是在猶太曆三月初一。若是這樣，從蘭塞到西奈大約花了四十五天的時間。
**西乃的曠野。**通常被認為是拉哈平原（er-Raha）。這是一個基本上平坦、灌木叢生的曠野，長約有3公里，寬不到1公里（見出3:1註釋），特別適合希伯來人聚集領受上帝即將宣佈的律法。這塊平原四面環山，形成了天然的露天劇場。其東南端聳立著一座幾乎垂直的花崗岩峭壁，提供了一個高大的講臺或講壇，使大家可以聽到耶和華的聲音。在峭壁下有一排小土墩以確定“界限”（第12節），防止百姓摸山。
律法就是在這樣一種莊嚴感人的環境中向以色列人頒佈的。人們注意到，世界上沒有一個地方能有如此奇妙的高山和平原的結合。《出埃及記》所描寫的場景和聲音在其中的每一個角落，都能被聚集的人群感受到。這是一個偏僻的地方，百姓可以完全單獨與上帝在一起，遠離一切吸引他們的心思意念偏離神聖事物的地方。以色列人要在西奈停留了十一個多月。除了領受律法和立約以外，還將建造聖所並進一步完善他們的組織。他們還有機會安靜地思考自己對於耶和華的責任。
上帝的子民需要這樣休息的時間，正如基督向門徒所提議的（見可6:31）。我們有保羅的榜樣。他曾獨自“往阿拉伯去”，可能就是去西奈（見加1:17）。我們每個人都需要有自己的西奈。在那裡的安靜和孤寂之中，上帝能為我們成就祂為以色列人所做的事情，顯示祂的旨意，指教我們明白，讓我們重新看到祂的尊榮。西奈是一個莊嚴的地方，人的心思將無法抗拒地得到提高，而與那無限的主進行交往。周圍肅穆壯觀的環境，象徵著律法的神聖性質。作為荒蕪不毛之地，西奈也深刻地提示：我們自己不能結出屬靈的果子榮耀上帝，也無法成就自己的得救。基督不是說過：“離了我，你們就不能作什麼”（約15:5）嗎？
**懷愛倫註釋（1–25節）**。《佈道論》232；《先祖與先知》301-304。
**懷愛倫註釋（1–2節）**。《先祖與先知》301。
**懷愛倫註釋（1–5節）**。《基督教育原理》505。

16.en: Thunders. Verses 16–20 deal with the manifestations of the divine presence upon Sinai. In revealing Himself to man the Lord employs various methods. To Elijah He came as “a still small voice” (1 Kings 19:12), to the prophet Daniel and the apostle John He used visions, to the disciples He spoke directly through His Son. To Paul, God appeared in ecstatic vision, the apostle hearing “unspeakable words, which it is not lawful for a man to utter” (2 Cor. 12:1–5). Here, when God would impress all with the importance and majesty of His law as the constitution of His spiritual kingdom, He appears with terrifying grandeur (Heb. 12:18–21).
16.zh:
到了第三天早晨，在山上有雷轟、閃電，和密雲，並且角聲甚大，營中的百姓盡都發顫。

第16-20節描寫上帝在西奈山臨格的場面。耶和華用各種方法向人顯示祂自己。對以利亞，祂用“微小的聲音”（王上19:12）；對先知但以理和使徒約翰，祂用了異象；對眾門徒，祂直接藉著祂的兒子說話。上帝在異象中向保羅顯現。使徒“聽見隱秘的言語，是人不可說的”（林後12:1-5）。上帝在這裡帶著可怕的威嚴顯現，為了使大家認識到祂的律法作為屬靈國度之憲法的重要性和尊嚴（來12:18-21）。
**懷愛倫註釋**。《福山寶訓》73；《先祖與先知》339；《成聖的人生》54。
**懷愛倫註釋（16–17節）**。《先祖與先知》304。
**懷愛倫註釋（16–22節）**。《救贖的故事》139。

7.en: The elders. It did not require many words to present the important issue or to answer the imperative question as to whether the people would accept the covenant upon the terms God required. However, before presenting these terms to the people, Moses summoned the elders, preparatory to setting the matter before the people (ch. 24:3; PP 303).
7.zh:
摩西去召了民間的長老來，將耶和華所吩咐他的話都在他們面前陳明。

提出重要的問題和回答百姓肯不肯按上帝所要求的條件接受聖約，並不需要多費唇舌。但在向百姓提出這些條件以前，摩西召集了長老，為把事情擺在百姓面前做準備（出24:3；《先祖與先知》第303頁）。
**懷愛倫註釋**。《基督教育原理》506；《先祖與先知》303。

6.en: Kingdom of priests. According to the divine plan and purpose the Israelites were to be both a royal and a priestly race. In an evil world they were to be kings, moral and spiritual, in that they were to prevail over the realm of sin (Rev. 20:6). As priests, they were to draw near to the Lord in prayer, in praise, and in sacrifice. As intermediaries between God and the heathen, they were to serve as instructors, preachers, and prophets, and were to be examples of holy living—Heaven’s exponents of true religion. In His coming kingdom God has a royal place for His royal children (Matt. 19:28; Luke 19:17– 19; John 14:1–3; Rev. 1:6; 2:26; 3:21; cf. Zech. 6:13). An holy nation. As a people consecrated to God’s service, they were to be unlike other nations. This was to be manifested outwardly by circumcision (Gen. 17:9–14) and inwardly by godliness (2 Cor. 7:1; 1 Peter 2:9). A holy God demands a holy people (Matt. 5:48; 1 Peter 1:16).
6.zh:
你們要歸我作祭司的國度，為聖潔的國民。這些話你要告訴以色列人。

**祭司的國度。**根據上帝的計劃和旨意，以色列人要成為君王和祭司的民族。在這個罪惡的世界中，他們要成為道德和屬靈上的君王，因為他們要戰勝罪惡的國度（啟20:6）。作為祭司，他們要藉著禱告，讚美和獻祭親近耶和華。作為上帝與外邦人之間的中間人，他們要擔任教師，傳道士和先知，並要樹立聖潔生活的榜樣，做上天真宗教的倡導者。上帝在祂未來的國度裡，為祂有君尊的兒女預備了最好的地方（太19:28；路19:17-19；約14:1-3；啟1:6；2:26；3:21；參亞6:13）。
**聖潔的國民。**作為獻身侍奉上帝的國民，他們與其他的民族是不一樣。在外面是藉著割禮（創17:9-14），在裡面是藉著敬虔（林後7:1；彼前2:9）。聖潔的上帝要求有聖潔的國民（太5:48；彼前1:16）。
**懷愛倫註釋**。《先知與君王》426。

10.en: Sanctify them. The Lord was about to proclaim His holy law in person, in order to remove all suspicion that Moses had anything whatever to do with its composition. Their appearance in the presence of God would require sanctification, without which none can see Him (Heb. 12:14). Sanctification is essentially a matter of the spirit, of being “pure in heart” (Matt. 5:8). The outward acts of preparation were designed to impress upon the people the need of preparing their hearts to meet God (1 Thess. 5:23; 1 John 3:3). Though to the Egyptians purification meant washing the body, including also shaving the hair from the head, and sometimes from the entire body, the Israelites seem to have purified themselves by washing only. Holiness is to be considered seriously each time we approach God. The unholy will not be rejected by Him if they come in repentance, accepting the grace of Christ. He accepts the sinner that He may make him holy, and thus qualify him for fellowship with God (Eph. 1:4; 5:25–27; Titus 2:11–14). Since the law that was soon to be given is an expression of God’s holiness, it was only fitting that the people prepare to receive it by sanctifying themselves. If the Israelites were to be the people of God, it was imperative that they appreciate the sacredness of this relationship. Therefore we can understand why God made the giving of His holy law an occasion to impress the people, deeply and dramatically, with the conviction of its sanctity and importance. This was particularly necessary since the Hebrews, oppressed by their Egyptian masters, had to a great extent lost a knowledge of the character and majesty of God. To day and to morrow. According to Jewish tradition this would be the fourth and fifth of the month Sivan, the Decalogue being given on the sixth. The two days’ preparation was to lend emphasis to the sanctity of the event. Wash. The rich might change their clothes when occasion required, but the people, in general, the poorer classes, having no change of garments, must wash those they wore (Lev. 15:5).
10.zh:
耶和華又對摩西說：你往百姓那裡去，叫他們今天明天自潔，又叫他們洗衣服。

**叫他們……自潔。**耶和華即將親自宣佈祂的神聖律法，以消除關於律法是摩西所寫的任何懷疑。他們來到上帝面前需要聖潔，因為非聖潔沒有人能見祂（來12:14）。成聖實質上是有關心靈的事，就是保持“清心”（太5:8）。外表的準備活動是為了使百姓認識到在心靈上必須為迎見上帝作好準備（帖前5:23；約壹3:3）。對於埃及人來說，潔淨不僅指洗澡，也包括剃頭，甚至是全身，但以色列人似乎只借著洗澡來潔淨自己。
每當我們接近上帝時，就需要認真考慮聖潔的問題。不聖潔的人如果悔改接受基督的恩典，就不會被祂所拒絕。祂接納罪人，使他成聖，以便與上帝交往（弗1:4；5:25-27；多2:11-14）。即將頒佈的律法是上帝聖潔的表達，所以百姓要潔淨，準備好接受它。如果以色列人想成為上帝的子民，就要認識到這種關係的神聖性。我們可以理解上帝把頒佈祂神聖的律法作為一個機會，使他們能深刻地認識到律法的神聖性和重要性。這是非常必要的，因為希伯來人受埃及奴隸主的壓迫，已經在很大程度上忘記了上帝的品格和尊貴。
**今天明天。**據猶太教的遺傳，這是西彎月初四和初五。十誡是初六頒佈的。兩天的準備是為了強調這件事的神聖性。
**洗。**富人可以在需要時換衣服，但窮苦的百姓沒有可換的衣服，所以必須洗穿過的衣服（利15:5）。
**懷愛倫註釋**。《證言》卷二611。
**懷愛倫註釋（10–11節）**。《服務真詮》279；《先祖與先知》304；《救贖的故事》138。

2.zh:
他們離了利非訂，來到西乃的曠野，就在那裡的山下安營。

希伯來人從利非訂朝東南方向前往西奈山。大多數百姓可能在上述的平原上搭起了帳棚。但也有些人可能在東北和西面鄰近的山谷中安營，從那裡也能看見西奈山。
**懷愛倫註釋（2–8節）**。《救贖的故事》137。

3.zh:
摩西到神那裡，耶和華從山上呼喚他說：你要這樣告訴雅各家，曉諭以色列人說：

**摩西到上帝那裡。**第3-9節介紹了上帝與以色列人所立的第一個約。摩西熟悉這個地區，因為上帝曾在這裡燒著的荊棘中顯現。上帝在這裡再次向祂的僕人顯現。這時他不再是一個孤獨的逃亡者，而已成為上帝子民的領袖。當摩西登上這座山時，腦海中一定是往事如潮。他對今後擔任艱難領導工作的信心一定得到大大的增強，因為耶和華所說他和他的以色列同胞將在這裡敬拜祂的應許就要實現了（見出3:12）。我們可以肯定摩西是帶著謙恭而又充滿信心的步伐登山的。
**雅各家。**提到先祖的名字是要人想起上帝賜給他的應許（見創28:13,14；35:11），和豐盛的福氣。這些福氣是耶和華現在向以色列人賜福的保證。自然是上帝提出來與人立約，因為人無權向上天提條件。這約不但表達了上帝的權威，也表達了祂的恩典和憐憫。是祂先尋找人類，而不是人類先尋求上帝（見約壹4:10,19）。
**懷愛倫註釋（3–4節）**。《先祖與先知》303。

4.zh:
我向埃及人所行的事，你們都看見了，且看見我如鷹將你們背在翅膀上，帶來歸我。

**埃及人。**值得注意的是上帝在頒佈律法以前先提醒人過去祂慈愛的證據。祂要這樣來贏得他們的信任；祂要加強他們對祂的信心，並鼓勵他們遵行祂的旨意。祂是用過去的福氣來保證將來的福氣。祂拯救以色列人出埃及，安全地帶領他們過紅海，賜給他們嗎哪，這一切都是祂要為他們成就之事的保證，只要他們繼續忠於上帝。沒有這種保證，西奈的恐怖景象是無法忍受的。
**如鷹將你們背在翅膀上。**正如老鷹將小鷹從巢中帶出，教它飛翔，用自己的生命保護小鷹一樣，耶和華也從埃及的奴役中救出祂的百姓，要把他們帶到迦南地。祂要用祂的“翅膀”把他們托起，保護他們脫離危險。正如軟弱無助的小鷹，在危險中依靠父母的力量和保護，軟弱、無助、恐懼畏懼的以色列人也可以相信上帝的大能（申32:11,12）。

9.zh:
耶和華對摩西說：我要在密雲中臨到你那裡，叫百姓在我與你說話的時候可以聽見，也可以永遠信你了。於是，摩西將百姓的話奏告耶和華。

**在密雲中。**上帝與人說話時，總得遮掩自己的榮耀，因為罪人承受不了（出33:20；約1:18；約壹4:12）。如果上帝披上人性，人體就成了遮掩。如果祂在燒著的荊棘中顯現，火就成了遮掩。在西奈，百姓中有許多人並不敬虔，尚未悔改，所以祂更要掩飾自己了。上帝從中發話的密雲，就是陪伴以色列人出埃及並指引導他們前進的雲柱（出13:21,22；民11:25；12:15；《先祖與先知》第301頁）。
**永遠信你了。**上帝向摩西顯現的目的之一，就是要給百姓一個無可辯駁的證據，證明摩西在他們面前是上帝的代表。
**懷愛倫註釋**。《先祖與先知》303；《救贖的故事》137。

14.zh:
摩西下山往百姓那裡去，叫他們自潔，他們就洗衣服。

摩西回到西奈山腳，遵照第10節的命令指示百姓為頒佈律法做準備。同時他一定吩咐在山腳建造了圍欄，防止百姓靠近。他在第23節中暗示這一工程已經完成。

18.zh:
西乃全山冒煙，因為耶和華在火中降於山上。山的煙氣上騰，如燒窰一般，遍山大大的震動。

**懷愛倫註釋（18–19節）**。《先祖與先知》304。

21.zh:
耶和華對摩西說：你下去囑咐百姓，不可闖過來到我面前觀看，恐怕他們有多人死亡；

本章的最後幾節再次警告百姓和祭司不要越過“界限”。這種重複暗示有人沒有把禁令當回事，準備“闖過”“界限”去窺視上帝的榮耀（見民4:20；撒上6:19；撒下6:6,7）。
**懷愛倫註釋**。《先祖與先知》339。

22.zh:
又叫親近我的祭司自潔，恐怕我忽然出來擊殺他們。

**又叫……祭司。**這裡特別提到“祭司”，暗示他們特別想越界。他們受訓要履行神聖的職責，可能認為自己與摩西和亞倫是平等的。他們可能不滿於被排除在上帝臨格的現場之外。難道他們沒有被任命為上帝與人之間的中間人嗎？
**自潔。**這條命令似乎表明，祭司們沒有把第10節的吩咐當作是針對他們的，因此沒有遵守。所以現在的命令特別針對他們。職務的聖潔不一定意味著擔任這個職務的人也是聖潔的。上帝的傳道人沒有任何對罪的豁免權，正如聖經所經常顯示的（見利10:1,2；撒上2:12-17；4:17）。本節和出24:5表明，在祭司制度建立以前，就已經有人被任命擔任祭司的工作（見《先祖與先知》第350頁）。

23.zh:
摩西對耶和華說：百姓不能上西乃山，因為你已經囑咐我們說：要在山的四圍定界限，叫山成聖。

由於已經執行了上帝在第12節中的命令，摩西向上帝保證說百姓不可能無意越入聖山的區域。

24.zh:
耶和華對他說：下去吧，你要和亞倫一同上來；只是祭司和百姓不可闖過來上到我面前，恐怕我忽然出來擊殺他們。

**下去吧。**上帝拒絕了摩西所說不需要再警告百姓的話。上帝知道祂僕人所不知道的事。祂指示要再次發出警告以防止麻煩的發生。
**你要和亞倫一同。**雖然這是第一次提到指定亞倫和摩西一起上山，但他似乎上一次也有上來（見第3,20,23節；參出10:1,3）。

25.zh:
於是摩西下到百姓那裡告訴他們。

摩西聽從上帝的責備，回到營中去警告祭司和百姓。

9.en: Eat not of it raw. This injunction was necessary in view of the fact that pagan peoples often ate raw flesh at their sacrificial meals. As to the prohibition against boiling the paschal lamb, see on v. 8. His head with his legs. Ancient Jewish expositors correctly understood this to mean that the lamb was to be roasted whole, including both head and thighs (v. 46). The purtenance. The viscera were to be roasted along with the rest of the lamb, the former first being cleansed. The preparation of the lamb typified the fact that the body of Jesus was not to be broken (see John 19:33, 36).
9.zh:
不可吃生的，斷不可吃水煮的，要帶著頭、腿、五臟，用火烤了吃。

**不可吃生的。**這條指示是十分必要的，因為異教徒吃祭物時經常吃生肉。關於不吃水煮的逾越節羔羊，見第8節註釋。
**帶著頭、腿。**古代猶太解經家解釋說，羊羔需要整隻地烤，包括頭和腿（第46節），這是正確的。
**五臟。**內臟先要清洗，然後與羊羔的其他部分一起烤。羊羔的製作預表了耶穌的身骨不被折斷（見約19:33,36）。

5.en: Without blemish. Freedom from blemish and injury not only befitted the sacredness of the purpose to which the animals were to be devoted, but was a symbol of the moral integrity of the One represented by the sacrifice. A devout spirit would teach a man that the “blind,” the “lame,” and the “sick” would not be acceptable to God (Mal. 1:8). The law afterward expressly prohibited the use of imperfect animals for obligatory sacrifices, though they might be presented as freewill offerings (Lev. 22:20–25). Freedom from blemish was especially important in a victim intended to typify Christ. A male. This requirement was made because the lamb stood in the place of the first- born male of the family. Of the first year. The animals to be selected were probably older than 7 days (see Ex. 22:30; Lev. 22:27), but should not in any case exceed the age of 12 months.
5.zh:
要無殘疾、一歲的公羊羔，你們或從綿羊裡取，或從山羊裡取，都可以。

**無殘疾。**無殘疾和無瑕疵不僅象徵獻祭的神聖目的，而且象徵祭牲所代表之主純潔的品格。虔敬的人自然會明白，“瞎眼的”、“瘸腿的”、“有病的”都不會被上帝所接受（瑪1:8）。以後頒佈的律例禁止使用有瑕疵的牲畜作為必獻的祭牲，但可以用作樂意的奉獻（利22:20-25）。用來預表基督的祭牲特別需要沒有殘疾。
**公羊羔。**因為這頭羊羔是代替家庭中長子的。
**一歲的。**所選的祭牲可能要大於七天（見出22:30；利22:27），但不超過十二個月。
**懷愛倫註釋**。《論飲食》20；《健康勉言》68；《歷代願望》50；《善惡之爭》473；《先知與君王》489；《先祖與先知》274，352；《成聖的人生》23；《證言》卷五541 。。

48.en: When a stranger. This injunction dealing with proselytes is similar to the one given in v. 44.
48.zh:
若有外人寄居在你們中間，願向耶和華守逾越節，他所有的男子務要受割禮，然後才容他前來遵守，他也就像本地人一樣；但未受割禮的，都不可吃這羊羔。

這條關於改信猶臺教者的指示與第44節的規定相似。

22.en: Hyssop. The Biblical hyssop, most authorities agree, is the gray-green marjoram, Origanum maru, now known in Palestine as za‘tar. This little plant with a pungent, fragrant smell, a taste something like peppermint, and masses of tiny white flowers, grows commonly on rocks and terrace walls. It has thick, hairy leaves and branches well adapted to holding liquids. It is used today as a spice or condiment and has some repute as a medicine. The Samaritans still use a bunch of za‘tar at their Passover ceremonies to smear the blood of the paschal lamb upon the door frames of their houses. In addition to its use in the Passover ritual, hyssop was employed on the day of the cleansing of a leper or a house (Lev. 14:6, 49), or one defiled by the dead, in connection with the offering of the red heifer (Num. 19:6, 17). Moreover, Moses used hyssop when he “sprinkled both the book, and all the people” at the ratification of the covenant (Heb. 9:19). Hyssop thus became symbolic of cleansing (Ps. 51:7). See also on v. 7. None of you shall go out. In this night of judgment there would be no safety anywhere except behind the bloodstained door. As for the Hebrew there was no assurance of safety beyond the protection of the blood of the lamb, so for the Christian there is no other salvation than the blood of Jesus Christ, the true “Lamb of God” (John 1:36; Acts 4:12).
22.zh:
拿一把牛膝草，蘸盆裡的血，打在門楣上和左右的門框上。你們誰也不可出自己的房門，直到早晨。

**牛膝草。**大多數權威人士都認同聖經中的牛膝草是一種灰綠色的墨角蘭（Origanum maru），如今在巴勒斯坦稱為za'tar。這種矮小的植物帶有刺激性的芳香，有點象薄荷，開著簇簇的小白花；通常生長在岩石和梯田壁上；其枝葉粗厚而多毛，極宜儲存水分。如今它被當作一種香料或辛辣調味品，還能用作藥材。撒瑪利亞人在逾越節儀式中仍用一束牛膝草（za'tar）把逾越節羔羊的血塗在各家的門框上。
除了用於逾越節儀式以外，牛膝草還用來潔淨大麻風病人或房屋（利14:6, 49），或被死屍玷汙的人，與紅母牛的祭有關（民19:6,17）。此外，摩西在立約的時候用牛膝草將血和水“灑在書上，又灑在眾百姓身上”（來9:19）。因此，牛膝草成為潔淨的象徵（詩51:7）。另見第7節註釋。
**誰也不可出自己的房門。**在這懲罰之夜，除了沾血的門內，沒有任何地方是安全的。對於希伯來人來說，羔羊的血是他們唯一的保障。同樣，對於基督徒來說，只有上帝的真羔羊才是唯一的拯救（約1:36；徒4:12）。
**懷愛倫註釋（22–23節）**。《服務真詮》403；《證言》卷五505。
**懷愛倫註釋（22–24節）**。《證言》卷六19。

27.en: Worshipped. Upon hearing these instructions the people, in the person of their elders (see v. 21,) “bowed,” literally, “made obeisance.” Thus they expressed their faith and manifested gratitude for the deliverance they were soon to experience.
27.zh:
你們就說：這是獻給耶和華逾越節的祭。當以色列人在埃及的時候，他擊殺埃及人，越過以色列人的房屋，救了我們各家。於是百姓低頭下拜。

代表百姓的長老們（見第21節）聽到這些吩咐就“下拜”，以表達他們的信心，和感激不久就要經歷的拯救。
**懷愛倫註釋**。《先祖與先知》274，279。

10.en: Let nothing of it remain. All the flesh was to be consumed at one meal lest putrefaction set in. Since Christ’s body was not to see corruption (Acts 2:27, 31; 13:35– 37), the symbolic lamb should not either. If the paschal lamb should prove too much for the number of participants, the remainder was to be destroyed, in order to prevent profanation of the sacred symbols of the body of our Lord Jesus Christ.
10.zh:
不可剩下一點留到早晨；若留到早晨，要用火燒了。

所有的肉都要在一頓吃光，免得變質。由於基督的身體必不見朽壞（徒2:27,31；13:35-37），象徵性的羔羊也不應腐敗。逾越節的羔羊如果吃不完，就要燒掉，以避免褻瀆我們主耶穌基督身體的神聖象徵。

6.en: The whole assembly. The head of each family was to offer the sacrifice for himself and for his family. Thus, no one outside the family intervened between it and God. This provision was in recognition of the fact that Israel was a nation of priests, as are Christians today (Rev. 1:6; 1 Peter 2:5, 9). The institution of the Levitical priesthood came at a later time (Ex. 32:26–29; Deut. 10:8). In the evening. The Hebrew words of this phrase read, literally, “between the two evenings.” This provision has been explained in two ways. Some have said that the first “evening” begins with sunset and that the second begins with the end of twilight. The medieval Jewish scholar Eben Ezra considered that twilight lasted for approximately 1 hour and 20 minutes. The command of Deut. 16:6, “Thou shalt sacrifice the passover at even, at the going down of the sun,” seems to support this view. Others have regarded the first “evening” as beginning when the sun begins visibly to decline from the zenith, at about three o’clock in the afternoon, and the second evening as beginning at sunset. In support of this view various texts have been quoted, such as Lev. 23:5; Num. 9:3, which refer to the Passover as being on the 14th of the month. If the slaughtering, they say, took place after sunset, it would then fall on the 15th of Nisan, not the 14th. The prevailing custom in the time of Christ agreed with this explanation; hence, Passover lambs were slain in the late afternoon, approximately the time when the true “Lamb of God” died for guilty man on the cross (1 Cor. 5:7; Matt. 27:45–50). Since time must necessarily be allowed for the preparation of the paschal meal, which was to be over before midnight, and since the word “evening” in Hebrew, as well as in other languages, is not limited to the time after sunset, the custom of slaying the animal in the afternoon may already have been in use long before the ecclesiastical authorities of the rabbinical age gave it their official approval. According to Josephus it was the custom in his day to offer the lamb at about three o’clock in the afternoon (Antiquities xiv. 4. 3).
6.zh:
要留到本月十四日，在黃昏的時候，以色列全會眾把羊羔宰了。

**全會眾。**每一個家長都要為自己和家庭獻祭。這樣就沒有外人在家庭與上帝之間干涉了。這個條例的依據是以色列是一個祭司的國度，正如今日的基督徒一樣（啟1:6；彼前2:5,9）。利未人擔任祭司是後來的事（出32:26-29；申10:8）。
**在黃昏的時候。**原文直譯為“兩個晚上之間”。有兩種解釋。有人說第一個晚上始於日落，而第二個晚上則始於黃昏的結束。中世紀的猶太學者伊本·以斯拉認為黃昏大約持續一小時二十分鐘。申16:6的命令：“當在……晚上日落的時候……獻逾越”似乎支持這種觀點。還有人認為第一個晚上始於太陽開始從天頂落下的時候，大約在下午三時，而第二個晚上是從日落時開始的。他們引用許多指出逾越節是在正月十四日的經文來支持這種觀點，如利23:5；民9:3等。他們說，如果宰殺是在日落以後，那就是在尼散月十五日，而不是十四日了。基督時代的習俗與這種解釋相符。因此逾越節的羔羊是在下午晚些時候宰殺的，大約是在“上帝的羔羊”為罪人死在十字架上的時候（林前5:7；太27:45-50）。
逾越節的晚餐必須有時間準備，所以下午宰殺牲畜的習俗可能在拉比時代的宗教當局正式認可之前早就存在了。逾越節的晚餐要在午夜前結束，因為希伯來語和其他語言一樣，“晚上”不限於黃昏。根據約瑟弗斯記載，他的時代習慣是在下午三點左右獻羔羊的（《上古史》xiv.4.3）。

13.en: I will pass over you. In passing through the land of Egypt to smite all the first- born of man and beast, the Lord would “pass over,” pasach, the Israelites. This word was transliterated into Greek as pascha, from which comes our English word paschal.
13.zh:
這血要在你們所住的房屋上作記號；我一見這血，就越過你們去。我擊殺埃及地頭生的時候，災殃必不臨到你們身上滅你們。

耶和華在巡行埃及擊殺頭生人畜的時候，將“越過”（pasach）以色列人。該詞在希臘語中譯為pascha；在英語中為paschal。
**懷愛倫註釋**。《復臨信徒的家庭》325；《給傳道人的證言》157；《證言》卷四21；《證言》卷五505。

3.en: In the tenth day. Though the lamb designated for the Passover feast was not to be slain and eaten before the 14th day of the month (v. 6), preparations for the feast were to be started 4 days in advance. A lamb. The Hebrew word is applicable to both sheep and goats, without limit as to age. However, by enactment the age was fixed (see v. 5) at one year, and a man was free to select either a lamb or a goat (v. 5). It is interesting that the Hebrews in general preferred a lamb to a kid, and with one recorded exception (2 Chron. 35:7), seem never to have used anything else for the Passover ritual.
3.zh:
你們吩咐以色列全會眾說：本月初十日，各人要按著父家取羊羔，一家一隻。

**初十日。**雖然逾越節的羊羔要到正月十四日才宰殺吃掉（第6節），但準備工作要提前四天開始。
**羊羔。**原文既指綿羊，也指山羊，年齡也沒有限制。但這裡的規定是一歲（見第5節），可以選用綿羊羔或山羊羔（第5節）。有趣的是，希伯來人一般都選綿羊羔而不是山羊羔。聖經只記錄了一次例外（代下35:7）。他們似乎從來不用任何其他的牲畜來守逾越節。

26.en: What mean ye? Moses assumed that the paschal ceremonies would arouse curiosity, and that each generation in succession would wish to know their origin and meaning. The ceremony is called a “service,” or task, inasmuch as it was performed in fulfillment of a divine command.
26.zh:
你們的兒女問你們說：行這禮是什麼意思？

摩西想到逾越節的儀式會引起後人的好奇。以後各世代的人都想知道這個儀式的起源和意義。這個“禮”是按上帝的命令實施的。
**懷愛倫註釋（26–27節）**。《歷代願望》77。

4.en: If the household. At a later time Jewish tradition fixed at ten the number of persons for whom one lamb was to be apportioned, and ruled also that all members of the family, men, women and children, must participate in the activities of the feast. The lamb, according to Jewish sources, was usually slain between the 9th hour (c. 3 P.M.) and the 11th hour (c. 5 P.M.). Every man according to his eating. When provision was made for those who were to participate, consideration was to be given to the amount each one would be likely to eat. Children and the aged were not to be counted in the same way as men in the vigor of life. Consequently, more than two families might unite for this purpose.
4.zh:
若是一家的人太少，吃不了一隻羊羔，本人就要和他隔壁的鄰舍共取一隻。你們預備羊羔，要按著人數和飯量計算。

**若是一家的人。**後來猶太教的傳統將分享一隻羊羔的人數定為十人，並且規定家庭的所有成員，不論男女老少，都必須參加這一節期的各項活動。猶太教的史料顯示，羊羔通常是在下午三時到下午五時之間被殺的。
**要按照人數和飯量計算。**守節之人的供品準備好以後，就要考慮每個人的食量。兒童和老人的食量和壯年男子是不一樣的。所以兩個以上的家庭可以一起享用。

11.en: Your loins girded. Ancient representations show Semites wearing long, loose garments, still the style in many Eastern countries. For work, or travel with a load to carry, the fore part of the garment is folded up and tucked into the girdle. Your shoes. Specifically mentioned, it not being customary to wear shoes inside the house or at meals. Some Jews have regarded these directions as of perpetual obligation. The general view, however, has been that these instructions applied to the first occasion only, when alone they served a useful purpose. Eat it in haste. Not knowing the moment they were to set out on their journey, and having to burn the bones of the lamb before their departure, they were to complete the meal in the shortest possible time. The Lord’s passover. With these words the significance of the meal is emphasized. The people were to realize that this was not an ordinary meal, nor was it merely a sacrificial repast such as they had known. For one thing, the lives of their first-born depended upon compliance with the regulations. It was, furthermore, the symbol of their deliverance, first, from bondage in Egypt, and second, in a wider sense they did not as yet understand, from the bondage of sin.
11.zh:
你們吃羊羔當腰間束帶，腳上穿鞋，手中拿杖，趕緊地吃；這是耶和華的逾越節。

**腰間束帶。**古代的繪畫描繪閃族人穿著寬鬆的長袍。許多東方國家至今仍保留著這種風格。為了做工或挑擔旅行，長袍的前部要折起來塞在腰帶裡。
**腳上穿鞋。**這裡特別提到這一點，是因為人們不習慣在家中或吃飯時穿鞋。有些猶太人把這些指示當作永久的義務。但一般人認為它們只適用於第一個逾越節，為了起行的方便。
**趕緊地吃。**他們不知道啟程的時刻，出發以前又要將羊羔的骨頭燒盡，所以他們要儘快吃完。
**耶和華的逾越節。**強調晚餐的意義。百姓應認識到這不是一頓普通的晚餐，也不是他們以前所瞭解的祭宴。一方面他們長子的性命有賴於遵守這些規定；另一方面，這象徵著他們脫離埃及的奴役，而且從他們還不理解的廣泛意義上來說，象徵著從罪的奴役中得救。
**懷愛倫註釋**。《歷代願望》77，653。
**懷愛倫註釋（11–14節）**。《先祖與先知》274。

8.en: Roast with fire. The meat of sacrificial meals was commonly boiled (1 Sam. 2:14, 15), but for the paschal lamb specific directions were given not to eat it raw or boil it, but to roast it (see Ex. 12:9). The reasons may have been that roasting was easier than boiling and that it would have been difficult to boil the “lamb” without cutting it into pieces, a procedure that seems also to have been prohibited (see Ex. 12:46; Num. 9:12; John 19:36). Unleavened bread. The roasted lamb was to be eaten with unleavened bread, for leaven produces fermentation, a natural symbol of impurity and moral corruption. For this reason leaven was also excluded from cereal sacrifices as defiling (Lev. 2:11). That Paul understood leaven in this sense is seen from his interpretation of the Passover as a type of Christ (1 Cor. 5:7, 8). With bitter herbs. That “bitter herbs” is the correct translation of a Hebrew word meaning literally “bitter [thing]s” cannot reasonably be doubted. Though it is not known what kind of “herbs” were used in Egypt, Palestinian Jews later used two varieties of lettuce, a kind of thistle, endive, and cress. Lettuce and endive are native to Egypt and Palestine. The latter may be found from the beginning of the winter months to the end of March, and lettuce in April and May. This probably accounts for the fact that the Jews considered these plants necessary ingredients of the Passover meal. Whatever bitter herbs were used, it is obvious that they were designed to remind the participants of their bondage and bitter suffering in the land of Egypt.
8.zh:
當夜要吃羊羔的肉；用火烤了，與無酵餅和苦菜同吃。

**用火烤了。**祭牲的肉通常是煮了吃的（撒上2:14,15），但關於逾越節羔羊的特別指示是既不可生吃，也不可煮了吃，而要烤了吃（見出12:9）。這可能是因為烤要比煮容易。羊羔不切成快是很難煮的。但切塊又是被禁止的（見出12:46；民9:12；約19:36）。
**無酵餅。**烤羊羔要與無酵餅一起吃，因為酵象徵不潔和敗壞。它被視為一種汙穢，不可用在素祭中（利2:11）。保羅對逾越節作為基督預表的解釋，表明他理解酵的這種含義（林前5:7,8）。
**和苦菜。**原文無疑指“苦的（東西）”。但不知道是埃及的哪一種“菜”。巴勒斯坦的猶太人後來用的是兩種萵苣、一種薊、菊苣和水芹。萵苣和菊苣在埃及和巴勒斯坦都有生長。菊苣的生長期從冬初到三月底；萵苣只生長於四、五月。所以猶太人用這些植物做為逾越節晚餐的配料。不論使用哪一種苦菜，都是讓吃的人不要忘記他們在埃及所受的奴役和苦難。
**懷愛倫註釋**。《先祖與先知》274，278。

1.zh:
耶和華在埃及地曉諭摩西、亞倫說：

**耶和華……說。**本章記錄了所謂摩西律法的第一個制度。應當注意，不論是這裡還是以後，制訂法規的並不是摩西和亞倫本人。摩西在出埃及以前和以後向以色列人宣佈的整個宗教和民事制度，都是上帝啟示給他的。他不是《摩西五經》中律法的原創者。這些律法雖然被稱為摩西律法，但只是上帝向祂子民傳達祂旨意的工具。
**在埃及地。**摩西的律法大部分是在西奈山頒佈的，所以摩西強調逾越節的禮儀是在出埃及以前制定的。
**懷愛倫註釋（1–51節）**。《先祖與先知》274-282。

2.zh:
你們要以本月為正月，為一年之首。

參出40:2,17；利23:5等，又稱為亞筆月（出13:4；23:15；34:18；申16:1）。亞筆月大致是在我們的四月，意思就是“穗月”，因為莊稼正好這時抽穗。被擄以後採用了巴比倫年曆的名稱，亞筆月成了尼散月（見尼2:1；斯3:7）。本節的新規定說明暗示以色列人以前的元旦是在另一個時間，可能是後來所稱的提斯利月，相當於我們的九、十月間。從此往後有了兩套曆法，一套是宗教的，一套是民事的。每一種曆法的正月都是另一個曆法的七月，但一般以尼散月為正月。亞筆月（“穗月”），現在成了宗教年曆的正月；提斯利月成了宗教年曆的七月，該月有西奈山所制定的重要宗教節日。以色列人從未放棄以提斯利月開始的民事年曆。它至今仍在猶太人中被使用。其存在可以追溯到整個舊約時期。猶太人認為上帝是在秋季創造世界的。

7.zh:
各家要取點血，塗在吃羊羔的房屋左右的門框上和門楣上。

**取點血。**血象徵著生命（利17:11）。作為祭物的要素，血一直被視為祭牲所預表之贖罪的特別象徵。逾越節的“羔羊”是要救贖各“屋”（原文又意為“家”），所以家裡要有顯眼的救贖記號。
**塗在。**就是用牛膝草蘸血塗在門框上（見出12:22）。《新約》清楚地告訴我們，塗抹逾越節羔羊的血，象徵著耶穌基督的死所成就的犧牲和贖罪（見彼前1:2；羅5:8,9；來9:13,14；13:12）。值得注意的是血不可灑在門檻上，可能指人不可“踐踏上帝的兒子”，“將那使他成聖之約的血當作平常”（來10:29）。使用牛膝草證明塗血被視為潔淨之舉（出12:22）。用牛膝草塗抹的做法只與潔淨有關（利14:49-52；民19:18,19；詩51:7；《先祖與先知》第275頁）。
以色列人在埃及沒有公共的祭壇，因此他們聚集過逾越節的房屋必須分別為聖，以至在滅命的天使經過時，裡面的人可以得到保護。所以在門楣和門框上塗血成了拯救的記號。上帝應許要放過每一個因信而塗上這個標誌的家。以色列人在迦南地定居以後，所有的人必須到上帝所指定的一個地方宰殺逾越節的羔羊並守逾越節，而不是在各城鎮和村莊（申16:5,6）。十二歲以上的男子都必須為此而來到耶路撒冷。在埃及，逾越節顯然是在特殊情況下慶祝的。我們不知道在門上塗血的儀式會不會長期保存下來，也許要經過一點改動。
**懷愛倫註釋**。《先祖與先知》274；《證言》卷五505。

12.zh:
因為那夜我要巡行埃及地，把埃及地一切頭生的，無論是人是牲畜，都擊殺了，又要敗壞埃及一切的神。我是耶和華。

鑑於許多動物都受到神化和崇拜，對埃及一切神的懲罰就容易理解了。有些家畜在以前的災難中已經遭殃；而現在所有頭生的動物都要殺死。這個災難不僅將影響神牛埃皮斯（Apis，是頭生的公牛），還影響許多被視為神聖的母牛，公羊，鱷魚，蛇和貓等。雖然這些動物中有許多並不具備商用或實用價值，但它們的同時暴死一定會使埃及人認識到它們的無能（見出7:17；8:2註釋；又見《先祖與先知》第333頁）。
**懷愛倫註釋**。《證言》卷六195。

14.zh:
你們要記念這日，守為耶和華的節，作為你們世世代代永遠的定例。

**要記念這日。**迄今為止的各樣吩咐都與出埃及前夕第一個逾越節的遵守有關。現在宣佈要年年記念遵守這個日子。以後還要加入其他內容，如從家中除去一切酵，逾越節後吃無酵餅七天，在節期的第一日和最後一日要聚集敬拜，把這些日子守為安息停工的日子等。
**永遠的。**原文為'olam。由於以色列人的得救具有永久的意義，以色列人只要一直作上帝的選民，他們就要永遠紀念這個事件。它作為一種預表，要一直遵守到那救我們脫離罪惡的實體耶穌基督的來到。“永遠”（'olam）是有條件的，取決於所指之事物的性質。它可以指無始無終，如上帝本身；也可以指有始無終，如得救之人的永生；還可以指有始有終的較短時間。本節是指最後一種含義。出埃及時所設立的逾越節要一直守到耶穌被釘十字架。

15.zh:
你們要吃無酵餅七日。頭一日要把酵從你們各家中除去；因為從頭一日起，到第七日為止，凡吃有酵之餅的，必從以色列中剪除。

**七日。**這七日始於正月十五日（利23:6；民28:17），或從正月十四日過後的晚上到正月二十一日過後的晚上（出12:18）。
**剪除。**聖經中有36種情形會使一個忽視某種宗教義務的人從選民中被“剪除”。我們不知道實際的情況如何，因為聖經沒有記錄具體的事例，也沒有指示如何執行這條命令。有人認為是指暴死，早死、或者永死。但也很可能只是指一個人被剝奪作為以色列人的權利。當一個人被“剪除”以後，他就會被視為一個外人，與聖約的福氣無份。
雖然一個人的錯行可能不為人知，但上帝卻是知道的。而且今後對儀文和道德律法的遵守並不能補贖過去所忽略或所犯下的罪。那個人要被隔絕，但不知道是由人還是由上帝來執行。這種“剪除”可能就是保羅在羅9:3中所說的事（見創17:14註釋）。
**懷愛倫註釋**。《歷代願望》77。
**懷愛倫註釋（15–22節）**。《先祖與先知》278。

16.zh:
頭一日你們當有聖會，第七日也當有聖會。這兩日之內，除了預備各人所要吃的以外，無論何工都不可做。

**聖會。**在亞筆月或尼散月十五日，就是逾越節晚餐過後七日除酵節的頭一日，百姓要聚集禮拜。這是聖經中第一次提到為此而召集的聚會。“聖會”指上帝為推進聖潔而明令召集的聚會。
**第七日。**亞筆月二十一日，即七日除酵節的最後一日，和第一日一樣，也要與除酵節的其他日子分別出來，舉行“聖會”（又見利23:4-8）。在以色列人其他的節期中，只有住棚節（利23:39-42）有這麼長的時間。
**不論何工。**在世界各國過節的時候，人們會放下那些會干擾宗教禮儀或當日職責的日常勞作。只有在希伯來人中，需要絕對禁止所有常規的工作。節期的第七日要歇下一切勞作，因此稱為“安息日”（見利23:15）。因為“安息日”意為“休息”。
**都不可作。**任何“勞碌的工”（利23:7）都不可做。但上帝並不想讓祂的百姓沒有飯吃，這是歡喜快樂的日子。所以維持生命和健康所必需的工作是可以做的。

17.zh:
你們要守無酵節，因為我正當這日把你們的軍隊從埃及地領出來。所以，你們要守這日，作為世世代代永遠的定例。

以色列人離開埃及的時候是沒有武裝，也沒有作戰準備的（《先祖與先知》第282頁）。關於第17-20節的各種用語和規則，見第14-16節註釋。

19.zh:
在你們各家中，七日之內不可有酵；因為凡吃有酵之物的，無論是寄居的，是本地的，必從以色列的會中剪除。

**寄居的。**指臨時或長期生活在希伯來人中間，卻沒有接受他們信仰和習慣的非以色列人。禁止吃有酵之物的規定對這些“寄居的”同樣有約束力。
**本地的。**就是以色列人。“本地”一定是指迦南地。自從上帝把它安排給亞伯拉罕的後裔以來，它就一直被視為以色列人的真家鄉（創15:18）。“本地人”指生來的以色列人，儘管所有摩西時代的以色列人事實上是在埃及出生的。他們是以撒和雅各的後代。以撒和雅各都是在迦南地出生的，而且從上帝那裡接受此地作為永久的家園。

21.zh:
於是，摩西召了以色列的眾長老來，對他們說：你們要按著家口取出羊羔，把這逾越節的羊羔宰了。

**眾長老。**見出3:16註釋。
**取出。**可能指牧人和剪羊毛者用鉤鉤住羊腿把羊從羊群中拉出來。關於羊羔，見第3節註釋。

23.zh:
因為耶和華要巡行擊殺埃及人，他看見血在門楣上和左右的門框上，就必越過那門，不容滅命的進你們的房屋，擊殺你們。

關於第23、24節，見第12-14註釋。

28.zh:
耶和華怎樣吩咐摩西、亞倫，以色列人就怎樣行。

摩西和亞倫所行的一系列神蹟給百姓留下了深刻的印象，所以他們毫不猶疑地立即順從了上帝的吩咐。命令是在亞筆月十日以前發出的（第3節），而逾越節的羔羊又不可在十四日以前宰殺，所以第28節包括了好幾天準備的時間。

29.zh:
到了半夜，耶和華把埃及地所有的長子，就是從坐寶座的法老，直到被擄囚在監裡之人的長子，以及一切頭生的牲畜，盡都殺了。

**到了半夜。**這一天以色列人雖然已經知道，卻沒有國王宣佈。這種不確定性肯定增加了他的焦慮。當摩西離開頑固的國王時，每一個臣僕無疑都為失喪長子的前景而驚恐。但幾天過去時間過去了。這個警告依然沒有實現，許多人，可能包括國王，都以為不大可能發生這樣的事了。但人們仍然擔心摩西的話語可能實現。
法老……的長子。如果以色列人出埃及時的法老是阿蒙霍特普二世的話（見《出埃及記》序言），那麼他的長子，即他繼位者圖特摩斯四世的長兄，就是在那個恐怖之夜被殺的。關於這件事，沒有任何聖經以外的記錄保持下來。古埃及人通常不記錄任何屈辱的事。但圖特摩斯四世卻留下了有關其兄長意外死亡以及他成為王儲的相關證據。他在吉薩的獅身人面像的石碑上記載自己清除了古碑上的沙土，以感謝他在其廕庇下意外地領受天命。在碑文中，他講述了有一天他在獅身人面像附近打獵。他正在其蔭下午睡，這位“大神”（獅身人面像）在異象中向他顯現並對他說話，就像父親對兒子一樣，說他將成為埃及未來的國王。這件事記在石碑上，證明圖特摩斯四世起初並沒有被指定為王儲。他也沒指望要當國王。他把自己的即位歸功於神明的介入。雖然沒有提到他的兄長，也就是原來的太子，但熟悉埃及碑文的人，肯定知道阿蒙霍特普二世這個從未被提到過的長子遭遇意外了。
我們不指望埃及文獻能為這個年輕人的遭遇提供一個滿意的答案。但如果假定阿蒙霍特普二世就是出埃及時的法老，其長子在第十災中的死亡將使小兒子，即後來的圖特摩斯四世，晉升為王位繼承人。為了避免將他的晉升歸功於希伯來上帝帶給國家的災難，圖特摩斯四世虛構並散佈了一個異象的故事。非正常的王位繼承通常被解釋為埃及偉大神明的干預。當哈特謝普蘇特繼承她父親王位的時候，她宣佈是阿蒙神生了她並命令她成為埃及的統治者。當沒有合法繼承權的圖特摩斯三世在一次神廟暴動中被立為王時，就公佈了阿蒙神的一個特殊旨意，授權他非正常地繼承王位。
**被擄……之人的長子。**與出11:5節“磨子後的婢女所有的長子”相對應。指貧富貴賤所有階層的百姓都遭了殃。但俘虜也確實有用作推磨人的（見士16:21）。
**一切頭生的牲畜。**“牲畜”的原文泛指一切“走獸”，如利11:2。此災不限於家畜。又見出11:5註釋。
**懷愛倫註釋**。《證言》卷四20。
**懷愛倫註釋（29–31節）**。《證言》卷一265；《證言》卷五119。
**懷愛倫註釋（29–33節）**。《先祖與先知》280。
**懷愛倫註釋（29–36節）**。《救贖的故事》119。

30.zh:
法老和一切臣僕，並埃及眾人，夜間都起來了。在埃及有大哀號，無一家不死一個人的。

**法老……起來了。**滅命的天使降臨西拿基立的軍隊（王下19:35），倖存者似乎到第二天早晨醒來才意識到。但當埃及的長子突然病死時，家家戶戶顯然都在半夜睡夢中醒來。
**大哀號。**見出11:6註釋。現在是那節經文的應驗。埃及遍地半夜的大哀號伴隨著要以色列人立即離開的催促（第33節）。埃及人現在肯定都害怕如果以色列人留下來的話，他們都將死亡。
**懷愛倫註釋（30–31節）**。《證言》卷四21。

31.zh:
夜間，法老召了摩西、亞倫來，說：起來！連你們帶以色列人，從我民中出去，依你們所說的，去事奉耶和華吧！

百姓的“哀號”無疑傳到宮中。國王意識到百姓要讓以色列人離開。由於國王的固執，全國所遭受的苦難已經忍無可忍了。他意識到必須立即採取行動，以避免更嚴厲的懲罰，於是就連夜打發官長（見出11:8）召見他拒絕再見到的（出10:28）可惡的希伯來領袖。
**懷愛倫註釋**。《歷代願望》77。
**懷愛倫註釋（31–32節）**。《先知與君王》369。

32.zh:
也依你們所說的，連羊群牛群帶著走吧！並要為我祝福。

法老已經完全屈服。他不僅命令他們立即帶著財產離開國家，而且向兩兄弟二人提出了了一個意想不到的要求。他們的話語既能帶來咒詛，也有可能帶來祝福。聖經中沒有記載他請求有沒有被接受，但提出請求本身，就證明他的驕傲被降卑到何等的程度。

33.zh:
埃及人催促百姓，打發他們快快出離那地，因為埃及人說：我們都要死了。

百姓的請求先是與哀號混雜在一起（第30節），很快就變成普遍的催逼了。希伯來人不僅要離開，而且得馬上離開。“我們都要死了”的哭號，說明他們害怕懲罰不會隨著長子的死而停止；他們擔心所有的人都要被殺；土地要被希伯來人奪取。

34.zh:
百姓就拿著沒有酵的生麵，把摶麵盆包在衣服中，扛在肩頭上。

這反映了埃及人的急迫。以色列人可能正要烤餅，準備出發。他們百姓雖然幾天前就得到摩西的通知，但似乎並沒有想如此匆忙地離境。他們還沒有準備好。他們雖然被告知在吃完逾越節羔羊以後要吃七天的無酵餅（第15節），但許多人要麼沒有把這個吩咐放在心上，要麼打算烤發酵的餅，在吃七日的無酵餅以後吃。但現在他們不得不滿足於無酵餅，即申16:3所說的“困苦餅”。

35.zh:
以色列人照著摩西的話行，向埃及人要金器、銀器，和衣裳。

**要。**希伯來語是sha'al。見出3:22註釋。

36.zh:
耶和華叫百姓在埃及人眼前蒙恩，以致埃及人給他們所要的。他們就把埃及人的財物奪去了。

見出3:22註釋。

37.zh:
以色列人從蘭塞起行，往疏割去；除了婦人孩子，步行的男人約有六十萬。

**蘭塞。**參出1:11。蘭塞主要是由以色列奴隸所建造的。據出1：11註釋，蘭塞很可能是泰尼斯城（阿瓦里斯）後來的名稱。在以色列人出埃及兩百年後，泰尼斯改命為蘭塞，是偉大的改革家拉美西斯二世命名的。該城的廢墟在阿拉伯語中現名桑哈傑爾（San el-Hagar），位於三角洲東北部，在蘇伊士運河邊的昆他拉西北約44公里處。
**疏割。**較早的註釋家錯誤地把這個以色列人離開蘭塞後的第一個停留處認定為比東。學者們現在普遍認為希伯來語的疏割譯自埃及語帖庫（Tjeku）。埃及文獻稱帖庫為一個邊境駐地。現被認定為土米拉特河谷（Wadi Tumilat）東部的馬斯古大廢墟（Tell el-Maskhuta），在泰尼斯或阿瓦里斯東南約51公里處（見上文）。
**六十萬。**註釋家們指出這裡的數字有些難解。如果只是指二十歲以上的男丁（民1:3-43），那麼總人口就可能達到數百萬。問題是這麼多的人，帶著他們的無數牲畜，是怎樣經過西乃半島狹窄的山谷而不至於延伸數百公里呢？更不用說他們如何能找到一個足能容納他們的大營地了。
有人指出聖經說以色列人相比較弱小，無法在一年之內佔領全地（出23:29,30；民13:28-33；申1:26-30；7:7,17-22）。
還有人解釋說希伯來原文的數字有些混亂。如把一百和一千放在一起，應該理解為一百乘以一千還是一百加上一千呢？（見本註釋卷三123頁）。
有人認為我們可能沒有準確理解希伯來文的“千”字（'lph或'eleph）。'eleph也可指“家”，如士6:15。還可以指“戶”，“宗族”等（撒上10:19；23:23；彌5:2）。另外，一個與'eleph輔音相同但元音不同的希伯來詞'aluph意為“朋友”或“支派首領”。因此有人說傳統上譯為“六十萬”的詞實際上是指“六百家”；更有可能與雅各一同進入埃及的十二家人，在215年後增加到了六百家（見創46:26,27註釋），而不是69個男丁在四代以後（創15:16）增加到六十萬男丁。
有人解釋說六十萬男丁是自然增長的結果，只要每一個兒子都象雅各一樣有十二個兒子。但據聖經記載，雅各的子孫沒有一個有十二個兒子。
'eleph的還可以指“軍事單位”（民31:5,14等）。因此有人說以色列的軍隊包括六百個軍事單位，來自各支派或宗族。
懷愛倫提到從埃及出來、死在曠野裡的有“兩百多萬人”和“上百萬的人”（《先祖與先知》第334,410頁）。這與六十萬的譯法（如出38:25,26）一致。
**懷愛倫註釋（37–39節）**。《先祖與先知》281。

38.zh:
又有許多閒雜人，並有羊群牛群，和他們一同上去。

關於“閒雜人”有好幾種解釋。有人認為他們是埃及人。他們目睹希伯來上帝的大能，想獲得侍奉上帝者的福氣，同時也想逃避法老的暴政。也有人認為他們是喜克索斯人或其他閃族餘民，曾被法老所扣押，現在抓住機會離開了埃及。他們當中至少有一部分是希伯來人與埃及人通婚所生（《預言之靈》卷一第243頁）。我們雖然不清楚此時加入希伯來凱旋之師的這些非以色列人的身份，但他們在後來的記敘中還會出現。他們總是最先後悔離開埃及，並貪戀埃及的美味佳餚（民11:4,5）。
**懷愛倫註釋**。《先祖與先知》315；《救贖的故事》120。

39.zh:
他們用埃及帶出來的生麵烤成無酵餅。這生麵原沒有發起；因為他們被催逼離開埃及，不能耽延，也沒有為自己預備什麼食物。

以色列人在疏割作了暫短的停留，為曠野的漫長旅程做最後的準備。聖經沒有說他們停留多久，但應該有足夠的時間烤制今後幾天所需的食物。

40.zh:
以色列人住在埃及共有四百三十年。

關於創15:13的討論指出，保羅在加3:17所說的話，以及其他的證據，均證明這四百三十年包括從亞伯拉罕蒙召離開哈蘭到雅各進入埃及的215年，以及從雅各進入埃及到以色列人出埃及的215年。在摩西的時代，巴勒斯坦被視為埃及帝國的一部分，所以當時的作者把迦南包括在埃及並不奇怪。七十士譯本的譯者不瞭解摩西時代的政治狀況，但覺得四百三十年應包括先祖在迦南居留的時期，所以他們特意譯成“住在埃及和迦南地”。關於進入埃及的人第四代要離開的預言（創15:16），及其應驗的記錄（出6:16-20），排除了對四百三十年的任何其他解釋。
**懷愛倫註釋（40–41節）**。《先祖與先知》282。
**懷愛倫註釋**。《歷代願望》32。

42.zh:
這夜是耶和華的夜；因耶和華領他們出了埃及地，所以當向耶和華謹守，是以色列眾人世世代代該謹守的。

就是吃逾越節晚餐的那夜。有關的指示已經發布（見第6-11, 14節）。以色列人永遠也不會忘記這恐怖與歡慶的交織。他們把那難忘的一夜作為一個民族的生日。

43.zh:
耶和華對摩西、亞倫說：逾越節的例是這樣：外邦人都不可吃這羊羔。

**逾越節的例是這樣。**在疏割發佈了一些有關逾越節的補充規定。因為在希伯來人的隊伍中加入了一些非以色列人。這些規定主要是針對外邦人的。通過這些制度，他們可以參加逾越節的活動並分享其祝福。
**外邦人都不可。**指想要保留其外邦人的身份而不受割禮的人。由於逾越節的意義在於記念以色列作為一個國家的誕生，外邦人參加這一節日自然是不合適的。

44.zh:
但各人用銀子買的奴僕，既受了割禮就可以吃。

以色列成為耶和華的子民不是靠著血統，而是藉著上帝的呼召。以色列註定要因此而成為萬國的福氣。，他們對外邦人不應該抱排斥的態度。他們應該歡迎那些願意與他們一起敬拜和侍奉上帝的人。這些在政治上和經濟上被吸收的“外邦人”，也應藉著割禮在宗教上被接納。這樣，他們就與上帝的百姓合而為一，並獲准參加逾越節的儀式了（見第48節）。

45.zh:
寄居的和僱工人都不可吃。

臨時的居民和僱工不可以吃逾越節的晚餐，因為他們與以色列人的關係隨時可能結束。

46.zh:
應當在一個房子裡吃；不可把一點肉從房子裡帶到外頭去。羊羔的骨頭一根也不可折斷。

這條規定說明逾越節的羔羊是基督的預表，約19:33,36表明，早期基督教會也是這樣理解。雖然那除去世人罪孽的上帝羔羊被當作普通的囚犯被釘死在十字架上，但祂的骨頭一根也沒有折斷。這並不符合當時的慣例。祂的兩個同伴都被打折了腿。正如被釘的基督與其他被釘的人有不同的對待，逾越節的羔羊也是以不同的方式準備的。一年中所吃其他羊羔的骨頭可以折斷以獲取骨髓。
**懷愛倫註釋**。《先祖與先知》277。

49.zh:
本地人和寄居在你們中間的外人同歸一例。

**懷愛倫註釋**。《先祖與先知》507。

51.zh:
正當那日，耶和華將以色列人按著他們的軍隊，從埃及地領出來。

本節屬於下一章的內容，是下一章的引言。
**懷愛倫註釋**。《先祖與先知》282。

27.en: Some of the people. As usual, there were some who either did not believe what Moses had said and wanted to see for themselves whether manna had fallen, or intentionally violated the commandment out of a stubborn desire to have their own way.
27.zh:
第七天，百姓中有人出去收，什麼也找不著。

和往常一樣，總有人不相信摩西的話，想親自看一看有沒有嗎哪降下，或者他們是出於頑梗和固執而故意違犯這條誡命。

13.en: Quails. Some commentators have explained the word translated “quails” as meaning either flying fish or locusts, but Ps. 78:27 makes it clear that “feathered fowls” are meant. It is now generally agreed that the word “quail” is correct. This quail is a game bird about 10 in. in length, the Coturnix communis, and belongs to the same order as pheasants, partridges, and grouse. It resembles the American quail. Ornithologists have reported great migrations of quail from Romania, Hungary, and southern Russia, across the eastern Mediterranean to North Africa. From Sinai thousands of quail a day have been exported to the markets of Europe. Many ancient Egyptian pictures show the people hunting quail with hand nets thrown down over bushes where quail are resting.
13.zh:
到了晚上，有鵪鶉飛來，遮滿了營；早晨在營四圍的地上有露水。

有些註釋家把“鵪鶉”解釋為飛魚或蝗蟲，但詩78:27說明這裡所指的是“飛鳥”。人們普遍認為“鵪鶉”是正確的。鵪鶉（Coturnix communis）是一種獵禽，身長約25釐米，和雉雞，鷓鴣和松雞屬於同一目，與美洲鵪鶉相似。鳥類學家曾報道有大批鵪鶉從羅馬尼亞，匈牙利和俄羅斯南部穿過地中海東部向北非遷移。每天有上千只鵪鶉從西出口到歐洲市場。許多古埃及的圖畫顯示，百姓撒網在鵪鶉棲息的灌木叢上捕捉鵪鶉。

15.en: It is manna. The two Hebrew words man hu’, thus translated, were long a puzzle to scholars. The word man could hardly be translated as the name of the heavenly bread, which appears first in v. 31. Some therefore translated the expression, “It is a gift,” but this again is far from convincing. The most probable interpretation is that of the LXX, “What is this?” a rendering supported by the words immediately following, “for they wist not what it was.” But since the Hebrew for “what” is mah and not man, it was suggested that Aramaic usage had influenced the text; yet the Aramaic man does not mean “what” but “who.” F. M. Th. Böhl, however, has shown that the form man was an old Semitic particle meaning “what.” It appears as manna, in the Palestinian Amarna Letters, documents written in the 14th century B.C. We may therefore conclude that this short phrase is properly translated, “What is this?” (LXX), or “What is it?” (RSV). This exclamation reveals the surprise of the Hebrews when they discovered the unfamiliar substance. The final solution of this problem, noted above, is one of the many evidences that the Pentateuch was not written many centuries after the Exodus, as so many modern scholars believe. Words and expressions like this, found only in documents from the middle of the second millennium B.C., would not have been used by a writer in the first millennium, for he would have been unaware of their existence at the time of the Exodus. The story of the Exodus was written by a contemporary of that great event, one who was acquainted with the phraseology of his own time, and who knew how to use it. They wist not what it was. This explanatory phrase shows that the preceding exclamation of the Hebrews was one of astonishment and inquiry. They could not have said, “It is manna,” when they did not know what it was, and Moses had to tell them that it was bread from heaven. If they had realized at once that it was the food sent them by God, there would have been no need for Moses to tell them so.
15.zh:
以色列人看見，不知道是什麼，就彼此對問說：這是什麼呢？摩西對他們說：這就是耶和華給你們吃的食物。

**不知道是什麼。**這句話指出下面疑問和驚訝的原因。他們還不知道這是什麼，而必須由摩西告訴他們這是天糧時，他們不可能說：“這是嗎哪”。如果他們立刻認出這是上帝所賜糧食的話，摩西就沒有必要再告訴他們了。
**這是什麼呢？man hu`。**學者們長期以來一直不理解這兩個希伯來詞的意義。Man很難譯為“天糧”的名稱。它第一次出現此在第31節中。因此，有學者把它譯為“這是禮物”，但也缺乏說服力。最有可能的的解釋是七十士譯本的“這是什麼呢？”，與前面的“不知道是什麼”相對應。但希伯來語中“什麼”是mah，而不是man，所以有人認為亞蘭語的用法影響了這句句子；但亞蘭語的man不是“什麼”，而是“誰”。F·M·Th·波爾（Bōhl）證明man乃是一種古老的閃族語小品詞，意思是“什麼”。該詞在公元前十四世紀所成的巴勒斯坦亞瑪拿書信中拼為manna。因此“這是什麼呢？”是正確的譯文，表達了希伯來人在發現這一陌生的事時的驚訝。
上述問題的最終解決，成了《摩西五經》不是出埃及以後幾百年才寫成的許多證據之一，如很多現代學者所認為的那樣。這類語句只存在於公元前1000-2000年中葉的文獻。公元前1000年內的作者是不會用這些詞句的，因為他不瞭解出埃及時的這些用語。出埃及的故事是當時代的人所寫的。他熟悉當時的用語，知道如何使用。
**懷愛倫註釋**。《服務真詮》200；《醫療佈道論》267。

29.en: See. The patience of God toward His stubborn people is amazing, and teaches an important lesson to us who tend to be impatient. Instead of always punishing Israel for their repeated murmurings and acts of disobedience, God condescends to reason with them, explaining the purpose of His requirements. The Sabbath was a holy day of rest, with which they were not to tamper; hence, the double portion of food the day before. Abide ye every man. The Israelites were directed to remain in camp on the Sabbath, and not to go out for manna or for any other purpose. Their time on that day was to be spent in rest at home and in meditation upon sacred themes. God had already instructed Israel to assemble for worship on days designated as “holy” (ch. 12:16), a practice that was consistently applied to other “holy” days (see Lev. 23:2–4, 7, 8, 21, 24, 27, 35–37). In postexilic times the Jews set up and enforced strict regulations concerning the leaving of cities or villages on the Sabbath. No one was permitted to travel farther than 2,000 cubits, or approximately two thirds of a mile. In the NT this distance is commonly referred to as “a sabbath day’s journey” (Acts 1:12). Endless, man-made Sabbath regulations have been strictly followed by orthodox Jews even since Bible times, with the result that the Sabbath, designed by God to be a delight (Isa. 58:13), became a burden.
29.zh:
你們看！耶和華既將安息日賜給你們，所以第六天他賜給你們兩天的食物，第七天各人要住在自己的地方，不許什麼人出去。

**你們看。**上帝對其頑梗百姓的忍耐是令人驚訝的。對於我們這些不耐心的人來說，這是一個重要的教訓。上帝並沒有一再懲罰以色列人不斷的怨言和悖逆，反而屈尊與他們講理，向他們解釋其要求的目的。安息日是一個安息的聖日，他們不應該踐踏；所以前一天為他們降下雙倍的食物。
**各人要住。**以色列人奉命在安息日留在營裡，不要為嗎哪或其他事出去。他們這一天的光陰都要用來在家休息並默想神聖的題目。上帝指示以色列人要在“聖”日聚集敬拜（出12:16），這和其他“聖”日的做法是一致的（見利23:2-4,7,8,21,24,27,35-37）。猶太人在被擄迴歸以後設立和實施了有關安息日離城的嚴格規定。任何人都不得行走超過兩千肘或大約一公里的路程。在《新約》中，這段距離通常稱為“安息日可走的路程”（徒1:12）。從聖經時代起，正統猶太人一直嚴格遵守有關安息日的數不清的人為規定，結果上帝所設立歡樂的安息日（賽58:13），反而成為一種重擔。

12.en: At even. Literally “between the two evenings” (see on ch. 12:6). Ye shall eat flesh. It was only on rare occasions that the Lord provided flesh for the Israelites. But two are recorded, the one here in the Wilderness of Sin and another at Kibroth-hattaavah in the Wilderness of Paran (Num. 11:31–34). Israel was not in actual need of flesh food, since the “corn of heaven” (Ps. 78:24) was adequate to supply all their needs.
12.zh:
我已經聽見以色列人的怨言。你告訴他們說：到黃昏的時候，你們要吃肉，早晨必有食物得飽，你們就知道我是耶和華─你們的神。

**到黃昏的時候。**直譯為“在兩個晚上之間”（見出12:6註釋）。
**你們要吃肉。**耶和華很少向以色列人提供肉食。聖經只記載了兩次，一次就是這裡汛的曠野，另一次是在巴蘭曠野的基博羅哈他瓦（民11:31-34）。以色列人實際上並不需要肉食，因為“天上的糧食”（詩78:24）足以滿足他們的一切需求。

31.en: The house of Israel. Some of the oldest versions, such as the LXX, the Syriac, and the Arabic translation, read “children” instead of “house.” It is possible that the reading “children of Israel” is closer to the original than “house of Israel.” Manna. No explanation of this name yet proposed has met with general acceptance. Some have suggested that it may mean “gift,” but it is more probable that the word owes its origin to the original exclamation of astonishment, man hu’, “What is it?” (see on v. 15). Like coriander seed. An herb, Coriandrum sativum, which grows wild in the Near East. Its aromatic fruit, called “coriander seed,” is used for seasoning and medicinal purposes. The color of the seed is whitish or yellow-gray. In Num. 11:7 it is compared with the bdellium (see on Gen. 2:12). Wafers. The Hebrew word thus translated appears only here in the Bible, and is of uncertain meaning. The LXX renders it by the word egkris, according to Greek literary sources, designates a cake made of flour, oil, and honey. The Israelites described the manna as tasting like cakes with honey (Ex. 16:31) and as if baked with fresh oil (Num. 11:8).
31.zh:
這食物，以色列家叫嗎哪；樣子像芫荽子，顏色是白的，滋味如同攙蜜的薄餅。

**以色列家。**有些最古老的譯本，如七十士譯本，敘利亞文譯本和阿拉伯文譯本將“家”譯為“人”。“以色列人”可能比“以色列家”更接近原文。
**嗎哪。**關於這個名稱的解釋，沒有一個得到普遍的認可。有人認為它是“禮物”的意思。但更有可能該詞源於上面感嘆的問句man hu'（“這是什麼呢？”見第15節註釋）。
**象芫荽子。**芫荽是近東地區野生的草本植物，學名胡芫（Coriandrum sativum）。其芳香的果實叫“芫荽子”，用作香料和藥物。種子的顏色呈白色或呈灰黃色。在民11:7中，嗎哪被比作珍珠（見創2:12註釋）。
**薄餅。**該詞原文只在聖經這裡出現，含義不明。七十士譯本譯為egkris，據希臘文獻，這是指一種由麵粉、油和蜜製成的糕點。以色列人說嗎哪的滋味如同攙蜜的薄餅（出16:31），好像用新油烤成的（民11:8）。
**懷愛倫註釋**。《先祖與先知》295。

5.en: On the sixth day. Here Moses indicates briefly the nature of the test implied in v. 5. Mention of “the sixth day” immediately reminds one of the sixth day of creation week (Gen. 1:31), the only previous occurrence of this expression, and thus of the fact that in six days God completed His work of creation (Gen. 2:1–3). Considered together with Gen. 2:1–3 and Ex. 20:8–11, this reference clearly points to the fact that the Hebrews knew of the weekly cycle prior to the giving of the law at Sinai (cf. Gen. 29:28). The seventh day, on which no manna fell, was “the holy sabbath unto the Lord” (Ex. 16:22– 30), and on it the people were to “rest” (v. 30). In Hebrew, the word Sabbath means “rest.” In conjunction with v. 23, v. 5 indicates that only the seventh day had a name, “the holy sabbath,” whereas the other six days were designated by ordinals, as the first, second, third day, etc. Twice as much. Twice as much manna was to fall on the sixth day, and they were to gather twice as much (PP 296). This weekly thought and activity required in preparation for the Sabbath was to be to Israel a lesson on the importance of the Sabbath day.
5.zh:
到第六天，他們要把所收進來的預備好了，比每天所收的多一倍。

**到第六天。**摩西在這裡簡要說明了第5節所暗示之試驗的性質。“第六天”馬上會使人想起創造周的第六天（創1:31）。這是該詞唯一在前面出現過的地方，從而使人們想起上帝在六天內完成其創造的大工（創2:1-3）。本節經文與創2:1-3和出20:8-11一起考慮，就可以看出希伯來人在西奈山頒佈律法以前，早已知道七日的週期了（參創29:28）。不降嗎哪的第七日乃是“向耶和華守的聖安息日”（出16:22-30）。這一天百姓要“安息”（第30節）。在希伯來語中，“安息日”的意思就是“安息”。把第5節與第23節結合起來，就可以知道只有第七天才有“聖安息日”的名稱，其他六天都只是以數字表示，如第一、第二、第三日等。
**多一倍。**第六天將降下雙倍的嗎哪。所以他們要收集雙倍的嗎哪（《先祖與先知》第296頁）。這種每週為安息日做準備的思想和活動，是要讓以色列人懂得安息日的重要性。

22.en: Twice as much. On the sixth day another miracle occurred. It had already been revealed to Moses that the people were to gather twice as much on Friday as on other days (v. 5), and this information Moses had passed on to the people, for “they gathered twice as much.” But nothing had as yet been revealed concerning its miraculous preservation, nor as to the fact that none would fall on the Sabbath. By gathering a double amount Friday morning the people had complied with instructions thus far given. But experience during the week had shown that any left over would spoil before morning (v. 20). This problem the tribal leaders now brought before Moses. Apparently, God delayed specific instructions concerning the Sabbath until this very time, since they had not been necessary earlier in the week.
22.zh:
到第六天，他們收了雙倍的食物，每人兩俄梅珥。會眾的官長來告訴摩西；

第六天發生了另一個神蹟。摩西蒙指示要百姓在星期五所收取平日的兩倍（第5節）。摩西已向百姓達給了這個信息，因為“他們收了雙倍”。但是關於嗎哪的神奇保存，以及安息日沒有降嗎哪，尚未給予啟示。百姓迄今為止均遵守上帝的一切指示。他們在星期五早晨收取了雙倍的嗎哪。但前幾天的經驗證明，剩下的嗎哪天亮之前都會腐爛（第20節）。各支派的首領現在把這一問題帶到了摩西面前。顯然上帝故意把有關安息日的指示拖延到現在，因為早一點發布並無必要。
**懷愛倫註釋（22–26節）**。《先知與君王》181；《救贖的故事》130。

26.en: Six days. These words are similar to those of the fourth commandment of the Decalogue. Here, mention is made not only of the Sabbath as a day of holy rest but also of the days of work preceding it. In God’s plan for man these six working days are of no less significance than is the Sabbath. They have been given to man for his own use. But the seventh day of the week is holy (v. 23). It should be spent in accordance with divinely given regulations as specified in the fourth commandment. The sabbath. Here the Hebrew text uses the definite article (see on vs. 25, 28). “The sabbath” is a sacred institution ordained at the close of creation week. Even then it was “the” Sabbath (ch. 20:11).
26.zh:
六天可以收取，第七天乃是安息日，那一天必沒有了。

**六天。**這句話與十誡的第四誡的相似。不僅提到了安息日是神聖安息的日子，而且提到此前工作的日子。在上帝對於人類的計劃中，這六個工作日的重要性並不亞於安息日。它們是賜給人類使用的。但是每週的第七天卻是神聖的（第23節）。應遵照上帝第四誡的規定度過。
**安息日。**希伯來原文使用了定冠詞（見第25, 28節註釋）。安息日是創造周結束時所設立的神聖制度（出20:11）。

4.en: I will rain bread. The patience and kindness of God toward His chosen people in these instances of murmuring is remarkable. Recognizing that their minds were still as servile and their faith as undeveloped as when they were in Egypt, God did not show Himself offended at their murmuring but sent help each time they were in trouble. In so doing it was His purpose to train them to trust their divinely appointed leaders and to have faith in Him. The phenomenon described here and elsewhere in the Bible (Deut. 8:3; Neh. 9:15; Ps. 78:23–25; 105:40; John 6:31) can be satisfactorily accounted for only as a miracle. The explanation of certain modern Bible expositors that the “manna” (Ex. 16:15) was the secretion of various plant lice is preposterous. Examining this so-called “manna” in 1927, F. S. Bodenheimer, of the Hebrew University of Jerusalem, found that various plant lice, cicadas, and scale insects feed on the tamarisk trees of the Sinai wilderness and excrete their excess carbohydrates in the form of honeydew drops. The latter evaporate into particles resembling hoar frost. This is supposed to be the “manna” that Josephus (Antiquities iii. 1. 6) said was still found on Sinai in his time. Acceptance of the narrative of Ex. 16 precludes the possibility that the “manna” of the tamarisk can have been the miraculous food on which the Israelites lived for 40 years. The heavenly manna was provided throughout the year, but ceased as soon as they entered the Promised Land (Joshua 5:12). The tamarisk “manna” is found on Sinai only during the months of June and July. The quantity of this plant “manna” is extremely small and could not possibly serve to feed many people, whereas God fed a whole nation with His manna for almost 40 years. Furthermore, the Biblical manna could not be preserved even to the next day, except on Sabbath (Ex. 16:19, 20), but could be baked (v. 23). In contrast, tamarisk “manna” can be kept for several days, but cannot be used for baking purposes, though it can be cooked. These points of difference show that acceptance of the modern interpretation, which explains the manna as a natural product of Sinai, means rejection of the Biblical record. This and other modern explanations, all of which are made with the purpose of escaping anything of a miraculous nature, do not deserve further consideration. That I may prove them. That the rain of manna was designed by God as a means of education is apparent from these words. The miraculous provision of food was to train the people to respect and obey His holy law.
4.zh:
耶和華對摩西說：我要將糧食從天降給你們。百姓可以出去，每天收每天的分，我好試驗他們遵不遵我的法度。

**我要將糧食從天降給你們。**上帝對祂發怨言的選民所表現的忍耐和仁慈是驚人的。上帝體諒他們的思維還處於為奴狀態，信心像在埃及時那樣尚未培養起來，就沒有因他們的怨言而生氣，而是在他們遇到困難的時候幫助他們。上帝這樣做是為了訓練他們信任祂所任命的領袖並且信靠祂。
這裡和聖經其他地方（申8:3；尼9:15；詩78:23-25；105:40；約6:31）所描述的現像只能用神蹟來解釋。有些現代釋經家把“嗎哪”（出16:15）解釋為各種蚜蟲的分泌物，這是很是荒謬的。耶路撒冷希伯來大學的F·S·博登海默在1927年對這種所謂的“嗎哪”進行了研究，發現各種蚜蟲，蟬和介殼蟲以西奈曠野的檉柳樹為食，並以蜜珠的形式分泌多餘的碳水化合物。這些蜜汁幹後就成為白霜般的顆粒，據認為就是約瑟弗斯（《上古史》iii.1.6）所說當時在西奈仍能找到的“嗎哪”。如果接受《出埃及記》第16章的記載，就排除了檉柳“嗎哪”成為以色列人生存四十年之神奇食物的可能性。天上的嗎哪是全年提供的，但一進入應許之地就停止了（書5:12）。檉柳“嗎哪”只在六、七月間才能在西奈找到。這種植物“嗎哪”的數量是極少的，不可能養活許多人；而上帝卻用祂的嗎哪供養整個民族達四十年之久。另外聖經的嗎哪不能保留到第二天（出16:19,20），除非是安息日，但卻可以烤的（第23節）。檉柳“嗎哪”則可以保存多日，可以水煮，卻不可以烤。這些區別說明，如果把嗎哪解釋為西奈的天然產物，就是拒絕聖經的記載。這種解釋和其他現代的解釋都是為了排除神蹟的成分，所以不值得考慮。
**我好試驗他們。**這句話說明降下嗎哪是上帝教育的手段。用奇蹟提供食物是為了訓練百姓尊重和順從祂神聖的律法。
**懷愛倫註釋（4–5節）**。《先祖與先知》294。

19.en: Let no man leave of it. God had provided the Israelites with food for which they had not labored, but He did not want them to become lazy. They must gather every day in order to have anything to eat. Furthermore, they must rise early, since the manna melted “when the sun waxed hot” (v. 21). Although there were no fields to plow or harvests to bring in, the fact that they must arise early to gather their food shows that God planned every detail of this phenomenon for the people’s benefit and training. Poverty and want are the reward of those who sleep late (see Prov. 6:9–11).
19.zh:
摩西對他們說：所收的，不許什麼人留到早晨。

上帝為以色列人白白提供食物，但祂並不想讓他們變得懶惰。他們必須每天收取才有得吃。他們還必須早起，因為“日頭一熱”嗎哪就消化了（第21節）。儘管不需要耕田，也不需要收割莊稼，但必須早起收取食物，這說明上帝為百姓的利益和訓練安排了這件事的每一細節。貧窮和缺乏是睡懶覺者的報應（見箴6:9-11）。

16.en: An omer for every man. The omer was the 10th part of an ephah (v. 36), that is, 2 dry qt. (2.2 l.). It is thought that the cup often depicted on Hebrew coins of the first Christian century represents the omer of barley from the new crop, presented at the Temple as an offering from the first fruits of the field.
16.zh:
耶和華所吩咐的是這樣：你們要按著各人的飯量，為帳棚裡的人，按著人數收起來，各拿一俄梅珥。

一俄梅珥等於十分之一伊法（第36節），也就是2.2升。據認為公元一世紀希伯來硬幣上經常所畫的杯就代表一俄梅珥新收成的大麥，作為田間初熟之物獻在殿裡。
**懷愛倫註釋（16–23節）**。《先祖與先知》295。

28.en: How long refuse ye? In speaking to Moses personally, God addresses the nation as a whole and its disobedient individuals in particular. This is evident from the use in the Hebrew of the plural form of the verb “refuse.” There had already been one act of disobedience the day the manna was first given (v. 20), but now one of a more serious nature occurred. God, addressing them as Judge, asks them to face the question of when He might expect sinful conduct such as this to end, and when they would learn that they could gain nothing by disobedience. The later history of Israel shows clearly how “long” it would take them to learn this important lesson. God’s question, “How long,” etc., implies that they had for a considerable time been doing this very thing—breaking the Sabbath, in full knowledge of the fact that they were doing what was wrong (see on vs. 25, 27).
28.zh:
耶和華對摩西說：你們不肯守我的誡命和律法，要到幾時呢？

上帝對摩西的話，實際上是對整個民族，特別是悖逆的個人說的。希伯來動詞“不肯”的複數形式說明了這一點。嗎哪賜下的第一天就有了悖逆之舉（第20節），現在發生了性質更為嚴重的事。上帝象審判官那樣質問這種罪行什麼時候才會結束；，他們什麼時候才會明白悖逆的壞處。以色列人以後的歷史表明，他們要花多長的時間才學會這個重要的教訓。上帝問“幾時”，暗示他們會長期明知故犯地干犯安息日（見第25,27節註釋）。
**懷愛倫註釋**。《歷代願望》283；《先祖與先知》297。

25.en: To day is a sabbath. Or, “Today is the Lord’s sabbath.” Although the definite article “the” does not appear in the Hebrew text, the grammatical construction permits such a translation. The same Hebrew word form, “a sabbath,” appears also in the fourth commandment, where the KJV renders it, appropriately, “the sabbath” (Ex. 20:10). In both instances, however, a strict translation would require that it be rendered “a sabbath.” At the same time “the sabbath” would be entirely permissible. There is nothing either in this text or in its context to indicate that the Sabbath was now given to the Israelites for the first time, as some have supposed. In fact, it is implied that they already knew of the Sabbath, but had grown careless in its observance (ch. 16:4). The Sabbath command was therefore renewed and its observance as a holy day reinforced (see on vs. 27, 28).
